(b) whether any comparison has been done regarding the average passenger fare amongst Bullet, Talgo and prevailing trains, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether study of cost comparison of Bullet train tracks with that of prevailing train tracks has been made, if so, the details thereof; and

(d) whether estimated time-line has been formulated for the Bullet train project, if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)


(a): Yes, Sir. Mumbai-Ahmedabad high speed rail corridor has been sanctioned for implementation at an estimated cost of ? 97,636 crore with technical and financial assistance from Government of Japan.

(b): As per Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) report, estimated average fare of high speed train services has 1.5 times the 1st AC fare of existing train services. Comparison with fare for Talgo trains is not possible at this stage in the absence of any plan of study in this regard.

(c): While cost of constructing a double line conventional track ranges between ? 15 to 25 crore per kilometre, the high speed track has been estimated to cost ? 140-200 crore per kilometre as per the JICA study.

(d): Mumbai-Ahmedabad high speed rail project is targeted for commissioning in 2023-24.

records.title: Decline in job opportunities in IT sector
details:
(a) whether there has been a decline in job opportunities in IT sector during 2013-2015, the details thereof;
(b) if so, whether it is anticipated that there will be more decline in jobs pertaining to IT sector in near future, if so, the details of plans of Government in this regard and reasons therefor;
(c) the details of the share of IT sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the country; and
(d) the measures being adopted by Government to arrest the decline in job environment of the IT sector?

(a) to (d): No, Sir. The direct employment in Information Technology (IT) and IT Enable Services(ITES) sector has increased from 32.6 Lakhs in 2013-14 to 34.8 Lakhs in 2014-15 with a net addition of over 2.0 Lakhs employees. Further, the total employment by IT-ITES sector is estimated to reach 36.8 Lakhs in year 2015-16. The technology automation has not replaced labour, but improved productivity and provided workers the time to focus on other tasks involving complex decision making and social interactions. Rather, the adoption of new technology creates jobs, increases productivity, and increasing the demand for skilled labour. The share of IT sector in India’s GDP is about 9.3%. Over the next decade, Indian IT-ITES industry would continue to create jobs.

records.title: Target and funds allocated for schemes for skill development
details:
(a) the details of the schemes announced by Government in 2014-2016, to promote skill development, along with the details of the funds allocated and utilized till date;

(b) if so, whether Government achieved targets in 2014-15 with respect to objective of the scheme/schemes, State/UT-wise details thereof; and

(c) whether it is a fact that the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) scheme also promotes skill development, if so, details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor?

(a) to (c) The are over 40 skill development Schemes/programmes being implemented by various Ministries/Departments. The multiple schemes under different Ministries have their own guidelines and there is no centralized record of all different programmes under different Ministries. During the last three years, i.e. 2015-16, 2014-15 and 2013-14, the number of trained persons (in lakh) is: 104.16, 76.11 and 76.37, respectively.

The short term skill development training programmes under the Ministry are delivered through National Skill Development Corporation under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) scheme which was launched in 2015-16. As on 28th July 2016, a total of 17.94 lakh candidates (under Fresh Training) have been enrolled, 17.93 lakh have been trained and 11.9 lakh have been certified (Annexure-I).

The Union Cabinet in its meeting on 13th July, 2016, has approved the new version with modification and continuation of the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) as ‘Skill Development Component’ of umbrella PMKVY to skill one crore people over the four years (2016-2020) with an outlay of Rs.12,000 crore.

The Government has formulated and launched a “Project for Livelihoods in Full Employment under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (Project LIFE-MGNREGA)” in April 2015 in convergence with Deen Dayal Upadhaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojna (DDU-GKY) and National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM). Project LIFE-MGNREGA aims at promoting self-reliance and improving the skill base of MGNREGA workers, thereby, converting them from being asset-less, helpless, unskilled worker’s dependent on Government support into fully employed entities with enhanced income.

details:
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE

(a)to(e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 173 FOR 8TH MARCH, 2011
(a) & (b) Computerisation of all allopathic CGHS dispensaries, except one in Bengaluru, have been completed and networked. CGHS does not have any general purpose hospital.
(c) to (e): CGHS beneficiaries can go to any dispensary within the same city and can also get medicines from that dispensary. If, however, any medicine has to be indented through the local authorised chemist, the same is issued only through the dispensary where the CGHS card is registered.
If a pensioner CGHS beneficiary is visiting a CGHS city outside of his registered CGHS city, then the beneficiary can avail all facilities enjoyed in his/her home CGHS city, including indented medicines. 
A serving CGHS beneficiary, if visiting another CGHS city, is required to take a temporary permit from his / her office for availing CGHS facilities including indented medicines in that city.

details:
(a) whether it is a fact that patients have to pay several hundred times more than 
the actual cost of the common drugs; and
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the names of the drugs which are being sold 
at the cost more than hundred per cent of actual costs by the sellers?

THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS(SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA)
(a) & (b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) and (b) OF THE RAJYA 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 274 REGARDING LIST OF DRUGS SOLD 
AT HIGHER PRICES FOR ANSWER ON 19-12-2003.
(a) & (b) No case has come to the notice of the National Pharmaceutical 
Pricing Authority (NPPA) where the patients have to pay several hundred times 
more than the actual cost of the common drugs. The 74 bulk drugs specified in 
the First Schedule of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO,95), and the 
formulations based thereon are under price control and their prices are 
fixed/revised by NPPA in accordance with the provisions of the DPCO,95. For a 
Scheduled formulation, a manufacturer is required to follow the price 
fixed/notified in accordance with the provisions of the DPCO 95. Para 7 of 
DPCO,95 gives formula for the calculation of the retail price of a formulation by 
NPPA and it provides for inclusion in the retail price of Maximum Allowable Post- 
manufacturing Expenses (MAPE) not exceeding 100% for indigenously 
manufactured formulations. MAPE means all costs incurred by a manufacturer 
from the stage of ex-factory cost to retailing and includes trade margin and 
margin for the manufacturer. Similarly, in case of an imported formulation, the 
landed cost forms the basis for fixing its price by NPPA alongwith such margin to 
cover selling and distribution expenses including interest and importer`s profit 
which should not exceed fifty percent of the landed cost. Prices of non–
Scheduled formulations are fixed by the manufacturers themselves keeping in 
view the various factors like cost of production, marketing/selling expenses, R&D 
expenses, trade commission, market competition, product innovation, product 
quality etc. The Government takes corrective measures where the public interest 
is found to be adversely affected.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

MINISTER OF STATE (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY)
IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL
(a) There has been a general increase in the cost of steel production over the last three years in the country.
(b) The major raw material requirement is dictated by the process route adopted for production of steel. In case of producers who operate on the blast furnace/basic oxygen furnace (BF/BOF) route, iron ore, coal/coke are used as the input-mix for producing finished steel. The producers operating on the Electric Arc Furnace and Induction Furnace (EAF/IF) routes use steel melting scrap, sponge iron and pig iron combination as the input mix to produce steel. Further, Limestone, Dolomite and , Ferro Alloys etc. are also required in varying degrees for production of steel. 
(c) In a deregulated environment, data on costs of various commodities required for the production of steel are not maintained by the Government. Costs of different inputs vary plantwise depending on factors like location, freight burden, availability of captive mining sources or otherwise, source of input- domestic or imported, etc. The estimated increase in the cost of some of the major commodities in respect of SAIL ,during the period April-Sept. `03 over 1999-2000 is given in the table below:

details:
(a) whether Government have formulated any scheme of promoting the 
use of gas in place of Naphtha as a fuel by urea producing units of the 
country;
(b) if so, the detailed outlines of the said scheme;
(c) total number of industrial units of the country under this scheme which 
are likely to use gas in place of Naphtha; and
(d) expenditure likely to be incurred by Government for the same?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (DR. CHHATTRA PAL SINGH)
(a) to (d): The primary consideration and goal of the new pricing scheme for urea 
units, made effective from 1.4.2003, is to encourage efficiency parameters of 
international standards based on the usage of the most efficient feedstock. 
Natural gas (NG)/ Liquefied Natural gas (LNG), being an efficient feedstock for 
the manufacture of urea, besides being a clean and cost effective source of 
energy, facilitating the switchover of the existing non-gas based urea units to 
NG/LNG for feedstock/fuel is being considered for Stage-III. Preliminary 
estimates have revealed that in case of naphtha based plants, the estimated cost 
of conversion would be of the order of Rs.20-25 crore, whereas in the case of 
FO/LSHS based plants, such cost would be of the order of Rs. 250 crore or more 
depending on the scope of revamp and engineering process. The cost 
differences are attributable to the size, vintage, technology of the plant etc. 
 At present, there are 14 non-gas based urea units. Their switchover to 
NG/LNG will depend on the availability of NG/LNG, delivered price of NG/LNG 
and the infrastructure available. The cost of conversion is to be financed by the 
respective units.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) US $ 7,50,000/-.
(c) & (d): The Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR) is housed in the headquarters of the World Bank at Washington, DC, USA. It supports a network of 16 International Agricultural Research Centres, also called as Future Harvest Centres. The mission of the CGIAR is to achieve sustainable food security and reduce poverty in developing countries through scientific research and research related activities in the fields of agriculture, forestry, fisheries, policy and environment and to realize this mission, the CGIAR have adopted a strategy comprising of the seven following elements, namely, (a) people and poverty focus, (b) modern science, (c) geographic priorities, (d) regional approach to research, (e) new partners in science, (f) task force approach and (g) catalytic role.
(e) & (f): The CGIAR, with its focus on public sector research, has been beneficial to the developing countries like India in the following ways.
1. Developing new varieties, particularly in rice, wheat, 
maize, pulses and nutrition cereals. 
2. Supply of Germ Plasm of rice, wheat, maize, pulses and potato. 
3. Technology Transfer. 
4. Support for Frontier Technology like GIS. 
5. Disease monitoring, containment and alerting across international 
borders.
6. Training of scientists by its various Centres has been beneficial in the 
 form of indirect benefit to the farmers.

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

ANNEXURE
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF UNSTARRED 
QUESTION NO.2483 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 
13.08.2003
The following PSUs/organizations are working under administrative control of 
Ministry of Power:-
i) Central Electricity Authority
ii) National Thermal Power Corporation
iii) National Hydro-electric Power Corporation
iv) North Eastern Electric Power Corporation 
v) Rural Electrification Corporation 
vi) Power Finance Corporation 
vii) Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. 
viii) Power Trading Corporation
ix) Tehri Hydro Development Corporation
x) Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd. 
xi) Damodar Valley Corporation
xii) Bhakra Beas Management Board
xiii) Central Power Research Institute
xiv) National Power Training Institute
xv) Bureau of Energy Efficiency 
xvi) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
Details about the above organizations such as their objectives/functions etc are 
available on this Ministry`s website (www.powermin.nic.in). However, main 
responsibilities entrusted to each organization are as follows:-
Central Electricity Authority: The Authority generally exercises such functions 
and performs such duties as prescribed under Section 73 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or 
by the issue of written directions of the Government in the matter of policy involving 
public interest under Section 75 of the Act. 
 The functions include rendering advice to Central Govt. on matters relating to the 
National Electricity Policy, formulation of short-term and perspective plans for 
development of the electricity system and coordination of the activities of the planning 
agencies for the optimal utilization of resources to sub-serve the interests of the national 
economy and provide reliable and affordable electricity for all consumers. 
National Thermal Power Corporation: The corporation is engaged in 
operating/setting up of thermal/hydel power projects and gas based power projects. 
National Hydro-electric Power Corporation: The corporation deals in 
construction, generation, operation and maintenance of Hydroelectric, Geo-thermal, Gas 
power Stations and Projects. 
North-eastern Electric Power Corporation: The corporation is engaged in 
development of the enormous power potential of the North-Eastern Region of the country 
through execution of power generation projects. 
Rural Electrification Corporation: The corporation, as a financial institution, 
supplements the resources of the SEBs/State Power Utilities/State Governments for 
various power projects including schemes for rural electrification, as are sponsored by the 
borrowing entities. 
Power Finance Corporation: The mission of the corporation is to function as the 
prime Development Financial Institution dedicated to the growth and overall 
development of the Power Sector. 
Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd.: The corporation supervise, operate and 
maintain Energy Transmission System. Establish/operate all Regional Load Despatch 
Centres and Communication facilities and participate in long distance trunk 
telecommunication business ventures. 
Power Trading Corporation: The corporation`s main function is to catalyse 
development of Mega Power Projects and other power projects by acting as a singly 
entity to enter into Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Independent Power 
Producers (IPPs) on the one side and Multipartite PPAs with users/SEBs under long term 
arrangement on the other. PTC has also been mandated for power trading to optimally 
utilize the existing resources in the country as also promoting exchange of power with 
neighbouring countries. 
Tehri Hydro Development Corporation: The corporation`s main function is to plan, 
promote and organize an integrated and efficient development of hydro resources of 
Bhagirathi river and its tributaries at Tehri. 
Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd. : The corporation`s main function is to execute hydro 
power projects in Satluj basin within Himachal Pradesh. 
Damodar Valley Corporation: DVC is committed to the economic and 
industrial growth of the Damodar Valley region which extends over an area of 24235 sq. 
kms in the States of Jharkhand and West Bengal. 
Bhakra Beas Management Board: The Board is responsible for the 
administration, operation & maintenance of Bhakra Nangal project, Beas Sutlej Link 
Project and Pong Dam including Power Houses and a network of transmission lines and 
grid sub-stations. 
Central Power Research Institute: CPRI functions as an National Power 
Research Organization and serve as a National Testing & certification Authority for 
electrical equipment used in power sector. 
National Power Training Institute: The institute`s main function is Power 
Training. 
Bureau of Energy Efficiency: The Bureau is responsible for spearheading the 
improvement of energy efficiency through various regulatory and promotional 
instruments. 
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission: The Central Electricity Regulatory 
Commission (CERC), an independent statutory body with quasi judicial powers, was 
constituted on 25-7-1998 under the Electricity Regulatory Commission Act, 1998, since 
`repealed` and deemed to have been constituted under Section 76 of the Electricity Act, 
2003. The functions of the Commission are: (a) To regulate the tariff of generating 
companies owned or controlled by the Central Government; (b) To regulate inter-state 
transmission including tariff of the transmission entities; (c) To promote competition, 
efficiency and economy in the sector; (d) To regulate inter-State bulk sale of power; (e) 
To aid and advise the Central Govt. in formulation of tariff policy and to frame guidelines 
relating to electricity tariff; (f) To associate with the environmental regulatory agencies 
towards developing policies and procedures for environmental regulations for the power 
sector; and (g) To arbitrate or adjudicate in matters relating to tariff.

records.title: CAPTIVE POWER PROJECTS IN PRIVATE SECTOR .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that captive power projects are operating in private sector for 
power production in the country;
(b) if so, the production capacity of these projects as on March, 2003 along with 
assessment with regard to the average production cost;
(c) whether it is a fact that power is being produced in this sector more than the 
requirement; and
(d) if so, the details of the said surplus power?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER
( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )
(a) : Yes Sir. 
(b) : The overall capacity addition programme for the country does not take 
into account captive power plants and as such, details of captive power plants being set 
up by private sector are not available. However, as per available information, the all 
India captive installed capacity (1 MW and above) of select industries was 16156 MW as 
on 31.3.2001. Unlike the independent power plants (IPP) set up by private sector, captive 
power plants are not required to obtain Techno-Economic Clearance of the Central 
Electricity Authority(CEA) and therefore, details of the cost are not available. Moreover, 
the cost of production of electricity from different projects varies depending on the size 
and the type of the power plant, cost of fuel used, location and technology used etc. The 
cost of production also varies from time to time depending on the quantum of power 
generated and off-take of surplus power, if any.
(c) : The power generated by captive power plant is primarily used by the 
linked industrial unit(s). Surplus power, if any, can be made available to the State 
Electricity Boards (SEB) on mutually agreed terms and conditions. 
On July 11, 2001, the Government of India (Ministry of Power) has 
circulated a Captive Power Policy prepared in consultation with the Central Electricity 
Authority, to all the State Governments and Union Territories, which recommends 
purchase of power by State Utilities from spare capacity in captive power plants. 
In the conference of the State Power Ministers held at New Delhi on 5th 
August, 2002, a strategy was evolved to tackle the power demand during the then 
prevailing drought situation. The strategy evolved included, inter-alia, increase of 
generation from existing thermal power plants and utilization of spare capacity of captive 
power plants, etc.
(d) : The performance of captive power plants is not being monitored by the 
Central Government. However, as per available information, the electricity generated by 
captive power plants during the year 2000-2001 was 59637.96 GWH out of which, 
3188.56 GWH was sold to State Electricity Boards / Utilities.

records.title: POST PRODUCTION LOSS IN AGRICULTURE SECTOR .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that 25 percent of post production crop is assessed to be lost in agriculture 
sector of the country;
(b) if not, facts in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that such loss could be minimized with the use of advanced 
technology; and 
(d) if so, facts in this regard and how it compares with loss in agriculture sector at international 
level?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)
(a)&(b): A Committee headed by Dr. V.G. Panse, in its report submitted in 1968, had estimated 
annual post harvest losses in the foodgrains in various stages at 9.33%. These included losses during 
threshing (1.68%), transportation (0.15%), processing (0.92%), rodents (2.50%), birds (0.85), insects 
(2.55%) and moisture (0.68%). A survey conducted by Directorate of Marketing and inspection, 
during 1973-74, had estimated post harvest losses in foodgrains to be about 5% out of which the 
storages losses were estimated at about 2.7%. A joint survey conducted by the Indian Agricultural 
Statistics Research Institute and Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute during 
1985-88 in Bulandshahar district of Uttar Pradesh had estimated total foodgrains losses at about 
4.12% due to different factors at various post harvest stages. Losses during storage and transit of 
foodgrains in the organized sector is however, less than 0.5% and 1.5% respectively.
 The high level Committee on Cold Storage and Storage constituted by Department of 
Agriculture & Cooperation under the Chairmanship of Shri JNL Srivastava, Additional Secretary, in 
its Report of February 1999 has estimated 25% to 30% post-harvest losses in horticultural produce 
depending upon the produce, season and the length of journey.
(c): Yes, Sir.
(d): In order to reduce losses to food-grains during the post harvest period, the Government of 
India had launched the Save Grain Campaign in 1969-70. The main thrust of activities of this 
Scheme is training, demonstration and publicity in the field of scientific storage of foodgrains at the 
farm level. Improvement of grain storage structure and popularization of scientific storage structures 
like metal bins, pucca kothis and RCC ring bins and other activities are carried out by the Save Grain 
Campaign for the benefit of farmers.
 Foodgrains stocks at commercial level are stored by various agencies on scientific lines 
during which necessary prophylactic and curative measures are undertaken to reduce losses.
 In order to promote scientific storage facilities in rural areas and to prevent quantitative and 
qualitative losses of the produce of the farmers, a Central Sector Scheme of construction/renovation 
of Rural Godowns titled `Grameen Bhandaran Yojana` is being implemented in the country since 
2001-2002. Under the Scheme, Central Government is providing investment subsidy to individual 
farmers, Self Help Group (SHG), Cooperatives, Corporations, Agricultural Produce Marketing 
Committees etc. Subsidy is provided @25% of the capital cost of the project not exceeding Rs.50 .00 
lakh for each storage project through National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development 
(NABARD) and National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). A higher subsidy of 
33.3% of capital cost not exceeding Rs.60.00 lakhs is provided for beneficiaries belonging to SC/ST 
and for North-Eastern States and hilly areas. So far under the scheme, NABARD has sanctioned 995 
projects with a capacity of 59.29 lakh tonnes. In addition, 1575 projects with a capacity of 7.42 lakh 
tonnes have been sanctioned by NCDC for construction of new rural godowns.
 A Capital investment Subsidy Scheme for construction of cold storage is being implemented 
by National Horticulture Board (NHB) through NABARD and NCDC to enhance the storage 
capacity for perishable commodities. Under the scheme, back-ended capital investment subsidy is 
provided to the eligible organisation @ 25% of the project cost not exceeding Rs.50.00 lakh per 
project and @ 33.33% of the project cost upto a ceiling Rs.60.00 lakh per project for North Eastern 
States. The Board has, so far, approved assistance of Rs.208.17 crore under the scheme for creation 
of additional storage capacity of 31.79 lakh tonnes.
 No study has been conducted to compare post harvest losses in India with other countries.

records.title: . IMPROVEMENT IN JUDICIAL SYSTEM
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a need to make comprehensive improvement in the 
judicial system of the country;
(b) if so, Government`s reaction in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that Government have received several suggestions in the 
past for this purpose; and
(d) if so, the suggestions received and the action taken by Government so far to implement
 these suggestions?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW & JUSTICE (SHRI P.C. THOMAS) 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The canvas of Judicial reforms is very wide, encompassing wide spectrum of issues
concerning different departments of me Government. A series of steps have been taken by 
the Government on the front of Judicial reforms. High Courts have been requested to 
implement the recommendations of the Malimath Committee to streamline procedure which 
will, inter-alia, expedite disposal of pending cases. Government have also been constantly 
reviewing the
accumulation of arrears in courts. Besides reviewing and increasing judge strength of High 
Courts every three years, Government have encouraged alternative modes of dispute resolution
including conciliation, mediation and arbitration. Special tribunals like Central
Administrative Tribunal, State Administrative Tribunals, Income Tax Appellate Tribunal,
Labour Courts, Consumer Courts etc., have been set up to expedite the disposal of cases. 
Information Technology is being used in generation of causelists, providing information to
the litigants/advocates etc., for speedy disposal of cases. A Pilot project has been
started for Networking and Computerisation of City Courts in the four major metrocities 
of Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata and Mumbai to serve as a model. The project is aimed at augmenting 
capacities of courts and speeding up their disposal through better court management with the
help of information technology.
Civil Procedure Code has been amended and the amendments have been brought into force with 
effect from 1.07.2002 which, inter-alia, limit the number of adjournments which can be granted
to a party to three, provide for speedy process service by speed post, courier services, fax 
or e-mail, authorise the court to fix time limit for oral arguments & provide for a number of 
other measures aimed at ensuring expeditious disposal of cases. Permanent Lok Adalats are being
set up for expeditious resolution of disputes relating to public utilities.
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme funds have also been provided for the use of 
Information Technology in the High Courts. Fast Track Courts have been set up to speed
up the trial of delayed cases, and in particular the cases of under-trials who have
been in jail for a long time.
State Governments & Union Territories have been requested to fill up vacant posts of 
Judges/Magistrates & supporting staff in District/Subordinate Courts. 
(c) & (d) Suggestions for improvement in the judicial system of the country are received
from time to time and these are considered by the Government on their merits. Such
suggestions relate to, inter-alia, speedy disposal of cases, appointment of Special
Judicial Magistrates, creation of Fast Track Courts, establishment of more Family Courts
and setting up of tribunals etc. The action taken by the Government have been enumerated 
in reply to Part (b).

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS
(SHRI VIJAY GOEL) 
(a) Yes, Sir. The Rashtriya Punarnirman Vahini Scheme was implemented to inculcate the spirit of patriotism and to raise the level of volunteerism in the society, especially among the youth. The Scheme provided an opportunity to youth to participate in the process of Nation Building and to involve the youth in various developmental programmes, which could bring about a socio-economic transformation of our society and the Nation.
(b) The Rashtriya Punarnirman Vahini scheme was initially launched on a pilot basis for two years in 80 districts of the country in the year 2000-01. However, due to various constraints, the scheme could be operationalised in 76 districts in 27 States of the country w.e.f. April, 2001. The scheme was extended to 40 more districts in 21 States in the month of June, 2002 . A statement showing the names of the states & the districts is annexed. 
(c) A total of 11,600 youth volunteers were involved in the scheme for two years i.e. for 2001-02 & 2002-03. Since the scheme was launched w.e.f. April 2001 for two years only on pilot basis, the scheme is not in operation now.

records.title: (clubbed) SUPREME COURT S CONCERN OVER MISUSE OF POTA
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether it is a fact that Supreme Court have expressed concern over the misuse of POTA in various States of the country during the hearing on Parliament attach case recently
(b) if so, whether Government have identified those States where POTA has been misused;
(c) if so, the details of the States; and
(d) what action Government have taken in this regard so far?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)
(a): The Supreme Court has not made any observation regarding the misuse of POTA in States during the hearing of the Parliament House attack case.
((b) to (d): It has been alleged from time to time in certain quarters that the provisions of POTA are being applied in cases where they should not be invoked, thus giving rise to apprehensions regarding the Act being misused. The Central Government has constituted a Review Committee under section 60 of the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002 to take a comprehensive view of the use of the said Act in various States and accordingly, give its findings and suggestions for removing shortcomings, if any, in the implementation of the said Act and to suggest measures to ensure that the provisions of the Act are invoked for combating terrorism only. This Review Committee has been notified in the Gazette of India Extraordinary on 4.4.2003.

quantity of ash in the same;

found in the imported coal; and

THE MINISTER OF COAL 
(SHRI KARIYA MUNDA)
(a): No, Sir, ash in coal of different seams differ widely.
(b): Coal produced in the country from different coal seams

moisture content.

(c): To reduce the ash content in coal the following
measures are taken by Coal India Limited:- 
(i) Adherence to the envisaged mining sequence laid out in
the mining method itself. 
(ii) Picking of oversize stone/boulders, extraneous
materials etc. 
(iii) Size reduction in coal handling plants/crushing
machines thereby segregating different size fractions and
eliminating the impurities of higher density. 
(iv) Adopting proper blasting procedure/technique for
reducing the possibility of ad-mixture of coal with over
burden materials. Keeping overburden benches sufficiently
advanced from coal benches in opencast mines to avoid
falling of over burden on coal bench/face. 
(v) Washing/upgradation of coal in coal beneficiation plants
thereby reducing the ash content in beneficiated coal.

records.title: PRICE OF FERTILIZERS IN INTERNATIONAL MARKET
details:
(a) Whether it is a fact that average prices of chemical fertilizers at the international 
market during the year 2002-03 were found less than that of average prices of the 
same in the Indian market; 
(b) the average prices of all the chemical fertilizers at the Indian market as well as 
international market; and
(c) what are the factors for which prices of chemicals and fertilizers are found higher 
in the Indian market?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICAL AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(DR. CHHATTRA PAL SINGH)
(a)&(b): The Maximum Retail Price (MRP) for urea as notified by the Government 
has been Rs.4830 per MT during the year 2002-03 which was lower than the average 
international price of $132.22 per MT (exchange rate of Rs.48.40). In case of DAP, the 
indicative MRP during the year 2002-03 has been Rs.9350 per MT, against this the 
average international price of DAP was $ 192.76 per MT and with the average rupee-
dollar conversion rate, the average import price of DAP was approximately the same as 
the MRP in 2002-03 in the country. As regards Muriat of Potash (MOP), since there are 
no exploitable reserves of MOP in the country, its entire requirement is met from import. 
On the other hand, there are no imports of complex fertilizers and Single Super 
Phosphate (SSP) in the country. 
(c): The main reason for the higher cost of production of urea in India is the costlier 
feedstock compared to the prevalent cost in the other exporting countries in the world. 
As regard DAP, the variation in the cost of indigenous DAP compared to imported DAP 
is primarily because of the reason that more than 90% of the raw material/intermediates 
required for its production are imported and their cost in the international market 
fluctuate depending on demand supply position.

details:
(a) whether it is a fact that 3,744 people are reported to be missing in Jammu and Kashmir
 during last three years;
(b) if not, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether any action has been taken by Government to ascertain the whereabouts of these
 people; and
(d) if so, the information gathered about these people so far and the number of persons 
out of the same who are supposed to be out of the country even now?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)
(a)&(b): As per the State Government of Jammu & Kashmir, an estimated number of 3744 persons 
have been reported to be missing till date.
(c)&(d): State Government has informed that most among the missing persons have reportedly 
been allured by mentors of terrorism and they are believed to have gone across the LoC/IB for
obtaining subversive training or are working with the terrorists as their guides/local trained
militants over here. In recent past a number of such reported missing persons had been 
killed in encounters with SF/Police thereby substantiating that these missing persons had 
become terrorists.
 In all the cases of missing/disappearance whenever the report is received at police
station level, immediate cognizance is taken. In all such cases, missing reports are entered 
in the records of concerned police stations and missing files opened. The police at Thana 
level also make all efforts to trace such missing persons. Information is shared at 
appropriate levels to ensure tracing out the individuals.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(a) whether Government have received any suggestions to completely transform the Food 
Corporation of India with a view to reducing the expenditure of the corporation;
(b) if so, when and wherefrom Government have received the same; and 
(c) the details of the suggestions and the extent to which reduction in expenditure is 
estimated to be achieved as a result thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI V. SREENIVASA PRASAD )
(a)&(b): The Administrative Staff College of India (Hyderabad), in its Report submitted 
in May 2001, has, inter alia, suggested that the Government and the FCI should consider policy 
changes and other measures to restructure the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to reduce the 
expenditure of the corporation.
(c): The major recommendations in the Report with regard to the restructuring of the FCI are 
that the Government and the FCI should consider the `unbundling` of the FCI operations, either 
functionally or spatially. This could be achieved either by dividing FCI operations by handing 
over procurement to State Governments, distribution to the railways and physical verification 
and storage to the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC). An alternative suggested is to create 
State level Corporations to carry out all the operations within the State. The Union level FCI 
would limit its procurement, storage etc. to the maintenance of the buffer stocks. The expected 
reduction of expenditure, on account of the proposed restructuring, has not been quantified in 
the Report.

records.title: FAULTY TELEPHONE SERVICES OF MTNL DELHI .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN)
(a) & (b): Sir, Fault rate in Delhi unit of MTNL is slightly on the higher side. The average fault rate per hundred per month in Delhi unit for the year 2002-03 (upto 31-01-2003) is 19.99, as against average of all India fault rate of 11.00 for the same period.
Not only the Telecom network of Delhi is one of the oldest where paper core underground cables still exists but due to very fast development of basic infrastructure like construction of flyovers, widening of road, digging by other utility services to maintain and meet growing demand of fast expanding population, there are more damages to underground cables. However, the fault rate for the month of February, 2003 has been brought down to 17.27 faults per 100 subscribers per month.
(c) The steps taken to improve the telephone services of MTNL are given in Annexure.
Annexure
 MTNL, Delhi has initiated several measures to reduce the fault rate as listed below:
1. All the electro mechanical exchanges & analog electronic 
exehanges in MTNL, Delhi have been replaced by digital electronic 
exchanges.
2. Paper core underground cables are being replaced by Jelly filled 
cables/Optical fibre cables with Digital Loop Carriers (D.L.Cs.).
3. For higher capacity primary cables and junction cables, duct 
systems has been introduced.
4. Rehabilitation work in respect of leading in cables and rewiring 
of multi storeyed building is being done.
5. Overhead wires are minimized by introducing 5 pair cables 
and wall Distribution Points (DPs).
6. The junction network has been completely transferred to optical 
fibre cable links.
7. Further improvement is being done by providing Synchronous 
Digital Hierarchy (SDH) systems connected on the ring architecture.
8. Subscriber loop length being reduced by planning more Remote 
Subscriber Units (RSUs)/Remote Line Units(RLUs)/Digital Loop Carriers (DLCs).
9. Wireless technologies like Cordect, Wireless in Local Loop (WLL) 
have been introduced. Faults are monitored on daily basis by senior officers.
10. Computerised fault reporting system is introduced, which helps in 
booking, testing and sending the faults to the concerned line staff.
11. In addition to this, line staff is provided with pagers for easy 
communication and follow up with the testing staff for speedy clearance 
of faults.
12. Managed leased Data Network system has been introduced to 
improve the performance of the leased circuits.
13. MTNL has liberalized the policy to replace all telephone 
instruments older than 5 years or repaired more than 2 times. This is 
being implemented in phases. In the first phase, instruments more than 
eight years old are being replaced.

based Political and Economic Risk Consultancy Limited with regard to corruption in Asian 
countries;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that India is said to be second most corrupt nation 
in Asia as per report; and 
(c) if so, the facts in this regard and Government`s reaction thereto?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS. (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)
(a): Yes, Sir. The Hong Kong based Political and Economic Risk Consultancy Limited (PERCL) 
coordinates a team of researchers and analysts in the ASEAN countries, greater China and South 
Korea. It provides consultancy to some of the leading corporations and financial institutions. 
(b): The PERCL invited responses from expatriate businessmen about their perception of the 
prevailing corruption in 12 Asian countries. India was one of the 12 countries surveyed by 
PERCL.
(c): The Government is fully alive to the need to root out corruption and to ensure 
transparency in its dealings as far as possible to build confidence among general public 
and also foreign investors. Government has introduced checks and balances for bringing 
more accountability and for ensuring efficiency in administration. The Secretary of each 
Department assisted by Chief Vigilance Officer has been made responsible for ensuring probity 
and integrity in his Department. Government has also taken several measures to ensure
transparency such as setting up of 90 Facilitation Centers, as on 1.12.2002 in various 
Ministries/Departments/organization to provide information and assistance to the public
regarding schemes and procedures of the organizations concerned. Also 71 Central Government
organization have published Citizen`s Charters reflecting the commitment of the concerned 
Ministries, Departments or agencies to provide services within the timeframe specified. Some
Ministries and Departments have also developed their own websites for promotion of 
e-governance. The Freedom of Information Act, 2002 has also been enacted for ensuring greater
transparency, openness and accountability in the functioning of the public authorities.

records.title: RESTRICTION ON TEXTILES IMPORT IN AMERICA AND EUROPEAN COUNTRIES H .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY)
(a) to (b) : Till December 31, 1994, the exports of textiles to certain developed countries including U.S.A., member countries of the European Union and Canada had been governed by bilateral textile agreements entered into between India and these countries under the aegis of the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA), outside the rules of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). With effect from January 1, 1995, the quantitative restrictions (import quotas) in the bilateral agreements under the MFA, are being governed by the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. Presently, our textiles and clothing exports face restraints in U.S.A., European Union and Canada. 
One of the central elements of the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) is the four-stage process for the progressive integration of textiles and clothing products as specified in the Annex to the ATC into GATT 1994 over a ten-year transition period. The integration process has however not led to any meaningful removal of quotas by the restraining countries so far. India has raised the issue of lack of progressive liberalization in international trade in textiles bilaterally and also at the World Trade Organization. In accordance with ATC, all the textile quotas would be phased out and textile sector fully integrated into WTO by 1st January 2005.
(c) to (d): India is not maintaining any restriction on imports of textiles as no restrictions were being maintained by it under the former MFA on 31 December 1994. Further, quantitative restrictions that were maintained for balance of payment reasons have been removed on all products including textile products by 31st March 2001.

details:

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) to (d) of RAJYA SABHA
STARRED QUESTION NO. 308 TO BE ANSWERED ON 12.3.2003.
(a): Yes, Sir. Production of coking coal has been decreasing
during the past few years. However, coking coal production
in this year (2002-2003) is likely to increase marginally
over last year’s achievement.
(b): Production of coking coal during 1999-2000 was 32.98
million tonnes in the country.
(c): Assessed coking coal production for the current
financial year 2002-2003 is provisionally estimated at
28.99 million tonnes.
(d): Principal reasons for decrease in production of coking
coal 
(i) dwindling of good quality coking coal reserves
mostly utilized in steel plants after washing 
(ii)
constraints of land acquisition and rehabilitation
resulting in restriction of production in ongoing mines
and also delay in implementation of new projects in
BCCL and CCL which are the major coking coal producing
subsidiaries of CIL. Sickness of BCCL is also an important
reason.

records.title: INDIAN ECONOMY .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS & PROGRAMME 
IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE
(SHRI S. B. MOOKHERJEE) 
(a) & (b): The compounded effect of achieving the targeted annual GDP growth rate of 
8.5 to 9 per cent over the next 20 years would result in a quadrupling of the 
real per capita income and almost eliminating the percentage of Indians living 
below the poverty line. This will raise India`s rank from around 11th today to 
4th from the top in 2020 among 207 countries given in the World Development 
Report in terms of GDP.
(c) &(d): With the above achievement in economic development, India would attain a 
level of development on par with Upper Middle Income (UMI) countries. One 
of the key parameters of the development of UMI countries is that the 
population below the poverty line is 13 per cent. India Vision 2020 aims not 
only to reach those reference levels of UMI countries, but to surpass them in 
many areas including poverty. 
(e): No, Sir. Indian Five Year Plans aim not only to increase incomes, but also to 
achieve significant improvements in social indicators.

The Armed Forces have the responsibility of defending the country against external aggression and safeguarding its territorial integrity. The manpower strength of armed forces is governed by the overall force structure based on country`s security needs and is not determined on the basis of the civilian population of the country. records.title: PRODUCTION OF CRUDE OIL .
details:
(a) the details of the plans proposed to increase the production of crude oil in the country; and
(b) the details of the percentage increase in the present production assessed after the implementation of these Plans?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)
(a) : several important steps have been taken to increase oil and gas production, which include the following :
(i) to improve the recovery factor from existing major fields by implementing Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) schemes; in particular Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has taken up 15 fields for this purpose at an estimated investment of Rs. 10,000 crore, which would also help in accelerating oil production from these fields. 
(ii) to increase exploration efforts through the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP). Under the three rounds of NELP, Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) have been signed for 70 blocks. 
(iii) to explore in new areas, especially in deep water and difficult frontier areas, as also explore in the deeper layers of the producing fields. 
(iv) to develop faster the newly discovered fields and to step up the use of new technologies for seismic surveys, work over, stimulation operations, drilling of wells etc. in producing areas.
(b) : As a result of measures taken the crude oil production has shown an increase of about 3.3% during April-January 2003 over the corresponding period in 2001-02.

records.title: (clubbed) ACCUMULATION OF WATER IN THE GANGA BASIN .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)
(a) to (d) As most of the annual rainfall occurs during 90 to 100 days
of monsoon season in intense spells, this results in generation of large
quantity of water in the Ganga river basin during the rainy season. In
1980 the Ministry of Water Resources (then known as the Ministry of
Irrigation) formulated a National Perspective Plan for Water Resources
Development which envisages inter-linkages among Peninsular rivers and
Himalayan rivers of transferring water from water surplus basins to water
deficit areas for optimum utilisation of water resources. The Government
of India established the National Water Development Agency (NWDA) in 1982
as an autonomous Society to carry out water balance and feasibility
studies for the National Perspective Plan. Himayalan Rivers Development
Component envisages construction of storage reservoirs on the main Ganga
and the Brahmputra and their principal tributaries in India and Nepal
along with inter-linking canal system to transfer surplus flows of the
eastern tributaries of Ganga to the west, apart from linking of the main
Brahamputra with the Ganga. As per the pre-feasibility studies carried out
by NWDA about 98 Billion Cubic Meter of water is available for diversion
to the water deficit areas from the tributaries of Ganga namely, Kosi,
Sarda, Ghagra and Gandak as well as from main Ganga at Chunar. The
Peninsular Rivers Development Component inter alia provides for inter-
linking of Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Pennar-Cauvery. The surplus waters
available in Mahanadi and Godavari as also from the tributaries of
Brahmputra via Ganga are proposed to be transferred to Cauvery basin after
meeting the requirement of drought prone areas in Krishna and Pennar
basins.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

while the inflation rate based on the CPI-(IW) remained between 3.2-4.7% during this period.
In fact Inflation rate based on the two indices converged in December 2002 to stand at 3.2%.

No Sir. In fact price rise in kerosene, flour and vegetables remained lower for CPI(IW) 
as compared to WPI for much of the year. Inflation rate based on the WPI and CPI(IW) for

details:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI AJIT SINGH)
(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. 453 FOR 20/12/2002 REGARDING PROMOTION OF CO-OPERATIVE 
SECTOR.
(a): Yes, Sir.
(b): Cooperative Sector plays leading role in the following economic areas:-
i) Disbursement of agricultural credit;
ii) Procurement and disbursement of agricultural inputs like fertilizer, seed, pesticides etc.;
iii) Marketing of consumer goods;
iv) Production and processing of sugar and oilseeds; 
v) Procurement and marketing of cotton; 
vi) Milk procurement and processing of milk products; 
vii) Development and marketing of fisheries; 
viii) Generation of employment in rural areas.
(c): Government of India has formulated the following plans to encourage the cooperative 
sector:-
i) Cooperative Reforms: The Central Government has enacted the new Multi State 
Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 which aims at providing full functional 
autonomy and democratic management to the societies. It has also formulated a 
National Policy on Cooperatives in consultation with the State Governments. The 
Government is now pursuing with the State Governments to implement the legislative 
and policy reforms in cooperative sector. This will enable cooperative societies to work 
as self-reliant and democratically managed economic enterprises.
ii) NCDC Programme for Cooperative Development: In order to improve the income of 
the members of the cooperatives and for creation of various facilities, the Central 
Government has a scheme of assistance to NCDC programmes for cooperative 
development. The NCDC Amendment Act has been amended to enable it to finance 
more activities allied to agriculture like animal husbandry products such as milk, meat, 
skin, wool, and the service sector and industrial cooperatives including goods produced 
by the cottage and village industries. The Central Government is implementing the 
following schemes through NCDC for promotion of cooperatives:-
(a) Assistance for cooperative marketing, processing, storage programmes in 
cooperatively under/least developed States/UTs; 
(b) Share capital participation in Growers Cooperative Spinning Mills; 
(c) Integrated Cooperative Development Projects in selected Districts; 
(d) Assistance to National Cooperative Federations; 
(e) Rehabilitation of Cooperative Processing Units proposed for 10th Plan; 
(f) Assistance for development of women cooperatives proposed for 10th Plan.
iii) Human Resource Development in Cooperative Sector: In order to professionalise the 
cooperative sector, the Central Government has initiated a number of human resource 
development programmes. It is implementing a Central Sector Scheme of Cooperative 
Education and Training through the National Cooperative Union of India (NCUI) and 
National Council of Cooperative Training (NCCT).
iv) Revamping of Cooperative Credit Structure: In order to revitalise and revamp the 
credit societies i.e. the cooperative banks, a scheme of revitalization of Cooperative 
Credit Structure has been finalised by the Central Government under which 60% 
financial assistance required would be given by the Central Government and 40% by the 
concerned State by way of bonds. This would be linked with cooperative reforms.

records.title: RECOMMENDATIONS OF GOM ON SUBSIDY .
details:
e:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Committee of Ministers, under the 
Chairmanship of Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission, had 
been constituted to give suggestions on fertilizer industry;
(b) if so, the names of other Ministers members in this Committee;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the said Committee has recommended in its 
report to withdraw subsidy from fertilizers; and
(d) if so, by when the subsidy has been recommended to be withdrawn?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)
(a) to (d): The Government had constituted a Group of Ministers (GOM) on 
8th March 2002 consisting of Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission, 
Minister of Chemicals & Fertilizers, Minister of Shipping, Minister of 
Commerce and Industry, Minister of Disinvestment, Minister of Agriculture 
and Minister of Finance. The name of Finance Minister was deleted from 
GOM on 24.9.2002. The GOM was constituted to examine the proposal for 
formulation of 7th and 8th pricing periods and to consider the Expenditure 
Reforms Commission (ERC)’s report on rationalizing fertilizer subsidies and 
give its recommendations. 
The policy parameters for 7th and 8th pricing periods were approved 
by the competent authority on 16.5.2002, which were communicated to all 
urea units on 4.6.2002. The GOM has, in its meeting held on 9.10.2002, 
finalized its recommendations on ERC report. Formulation of new pricing 
policy for urea units based on GOM’s recommendations for replacing the 
existing Retention Price Scheme is under consideration of the Government. 
The proposed policy will be in the shape of Group Concession Scheme and 
is proposed to be introduced w.e.f 1.4.2003. The new policy will aim at 
greater transparency, uniformity and efficiency in subsidy disbursements to 
urea units and will induce urea manufacturers to take cost reduction 
measures on their own and be competitive.

 The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi have not made any formal study of the time taken in adjudication of rape cases. However, it normally takes the courts 1-4 years to decide such cases.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM RAJU )
(a): To check the alleged starvation deaths Central teams were sent to Rajasthan and Orissa.
(b): Shri B.B. Patnaik, Commercial Manager (CM), Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), Head 
Quarter New Delhi & Dr. Ashok Kumar, Deputy Director, Storage and Research, Department of Food 
and Public Distribution visited Rajasthan on 22nd & 23rd October, 2002.
 Shri B.B. Patnaik, CM, CWC, HQ, New Delhi, Shri K.M. Vaghela, Deputy Director, Department
of Food & Public Distribution, New Delhi, Shri P.K. Mahapatra, Senior Regional Manager, and 
Shri Y.K. Das, Regional Manager, Food Corporation of India, Bhubaneswar, Orissa visited Orissa
on 1st September, 2002.
(c): The team that visited Rajasthan has reported that the deaths in Suvans and Gangapur
villages of Baran district could have been due to starvation coupled with malnutrition and lack 
of timely medical attention. The team observed wide-spread hardship, huger and malnutrition in
remote areas due, mainly, to the failure of the Public Distribution System and the absence of 
employment opportunities.
 As per the finding of the team that visited Orissa, the alleged deaths in Gajakupalli
village of Muniguda Block in Rayagada District and Kuladera village of Keonjhar District did not
appear to be due to starvation. Adequate quantity of foodgrains of fair average quality(FAQ)
was found available at the fair price shops. However, it was noticed that certain poor families
in utter distress were burrowing money from village money lenders by mortgaging their ration 
cards. The ration cards in most cases were with incomplete details.

beneficial than the big power projects?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI ANANT G. GEETE )
(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
 STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) 
OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 317 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE 
RAJYA SABHA ON 11.12.2002 REGARDING CONSTRUCTION 
OF SMALL HYDRO-POWER PROJECTS.
(a) to (c) : There is no proposal to give incentives specifically for hydro power 
projects of 50 to 75 Megawatts capacity. However, the Ministry of Non-
Conventional Energy Sources have announced various incentive schemes for the 
development of small hydro power projects up to 25 MW capacity. Details of these 
incentives are given in Annex.
(d) : The benefits and tariffs of smaller hydro-electric projects are not 
necessarily better than those of larger projects. The costs, benefits and tariffs are 
site specific for hydroelectric projects. Small hydro projects can be developed in a 
shorter time frame as well as at a lower capital investment and involve lesser 
environment and rehabilitation & resettlement problems. Small and mini hydro 
projects have the potential to provide energy in remote and hilly areas where 
extension of grid system is either not possible or is un-economical. Larger 
projects, particularly multi purpose projects provide tremendous benefits in the 
nature of power, irrigation, drinking water, flood control, and are also advantageous 
in terms of economy of scale besides providing peaking power even in the lean 
season, and opening up other economic opportunities in the areas of their location.

records.title: (clubbed) DISTRIBUTION AND TRANSMISSION LOSSES .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether it is a fact that power shortage in peak as well as general hours 
in the country can be brought to negligible level by bringing the losses in its 
distribution and transmission system at the international level;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that the power distribution and 
transmission losses at international level have been assessed at six per cent 
only; and
(c) if not, the percentage thereof and what is the Government`s time-
bound scheme for bringing the above said power losses to the international 
level?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI ANANT G. GEETE )
(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
 STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED 
QUESTION NO. 313 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 
11.12.2002 REGARDING DISTRIBUTION AND TRANSMISSION LOSSES.
(a) : Yes, Sir. 
(b) & (c) : The transmission and distribution (T&D) losses in the developed 
countries of the world are in the range of 6-11%. The level of T&D losses in the 
country is around 31% and is higher than that of the developed countries of the 
world. While the losses in Extra High Voltage network (EHV) about 4-5%, bulk of 
the losses occur in the sub-transmission and distribution systems. 
The reasons for high T&D losses in the country are on account of:
i. weak and inadequate sub-transmission and distribution system due to 
low priority being given to these works
ii. large scale rural electrification programme undertaken in the country 
resulting in long lines and extension of distribution network without 
strengthening the back-up transmission and sub-transmission system
iii. too many transformation stages resulting in higher component of 
transformation losses
iv. improper load management resulting in over loading of system
v. low power factor due to pumping load in rural areas, and air 
conditioners, coolers and industrial loads in urban areas and 
inadequate reactive compensation at the load points
vi. low quality of construction and inadequate maintenance of equipment
vii. unmetered supply to agricultural pumps and small domestic 
connections to weaker sections of the society in some states
viii. pilferage and theft of energy. 
In order to achieve commercial viability, Ministry of Power has 
formulated a six level intervention strategy that encompasses initiatives at national 
level, state level, SEB/Utility level, distribution circle level, feeder level and the 
consumer level. This six level intervention strategy will focus on accountability, 
deliverability and performance at all levels to rejuvenate the distribution sector, 
where the maximum interface with the ultimate customers exists, the highest value 
addition occurs, and eighty percent of total T&D losses including nearly all the 
commercial losses take place. 
To give a strong impetus to the process of reforms, the Ministry of 
Power organized a Conference of Chief Ministers/ Power Ministers on Power 
Sector Reforms on 3rd March 2001. It was emphasised inter alia that commercial 
viability has to be achieved in distribution in 2-3 years through any or all of the 
following
- Creating profit centres with full accountability 
- Handing over local distribution to Panchayats/Local 
Bodies/Franchisees/ Users Association, wherever necessary
- Privatisation of distribution
25 States have signed Memorandum of Understanding for undertaking 
reforms and restructuring in a time bound manner and linking the support of 
Government of India to achievement of predetermined milestones. To bring about 
commitment towards distribution reforms, State Electricity Boards/Utilities have 
been asked to sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) with Ministry of Power as 
a pre-requisite for release of Accelerated Power Development and Reforms 
Programme (APDRP) funds. Till now 18 States have signed the MoA. A number of 
States have enacted anti-electricity theft legislation. 
To reduce the transmission and distribution losses in a phased manner, 
the Government of India has launched the APDRP in February 2000. The APDRP 
includes upgradation of sub-transmission and distribution network, energy audit 
activities and metering in a phased manner.

records.title: REQUIREMENT OF JUDGES .
details:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government consider it necessary to increase the number 
of Judges in view of the increasing population of the country;
(b) if so, the estimated number of Judges required in the country at present; and
(c) the total number of Judges in position at present?

MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI K. JANA KRISHNAMURTHI) 
(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT WITH REGARD TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 277 TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, THE 
9th DECEMBER, 2002 
(a) The Judge strength in Supreme Court is as per the Constitution of India. The Judge 
strength in the High Courts is reviewed once in three years as per prescribed norms on the 
basis of figures of institution, disposal and pendency of cases in each High Court. As regards 
District and Subordinate Courts, the Judge strength is worked out by State Governments in 
consultation with the concerned High Courts.
However, the Supreme Court, in its Judgment of 21st March, 2002, in All India Judges` 
Association & Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors, has directed that an increase in the judge 
strength from the existing ratio of 10.5 or 13 per 10 lakh people to 50 judges per 10 
lakh people should be effected and implemented within a period of five years in a phased 
manner to be determined and directed by the Union Ministry of Law. The Central Government 
has filed applications before the Supreme Court, seeking modification of its directions for 
increase in Judge strength on the basis of population in respect of Union territories and 
permit the Union Government to determine the appropriate judge strength based on the relevant 
factors including pendency of cases. The matter is sub judice. 
(b) An estimated 51,351 Judges would be required to be in position on the basis of 
population as per Census 2001. 
(c) As per available information, the total number of Judges in position at
present is 15,095.

 Governments for purchasing sugarcane;
(b) if so, the prices fixed by the Central Government and the sugarcane growing States at

MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI SHARAD YADAV )
(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO.258 DUE FOR
ANSWER ON 05-12-2002 IN THE RAJYA SABHA.
 Under the provisions of the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, the power to fix the 
sugarcane prices vests with the Central Government. The Central Government, in terms of 
clause 3 of the said Order, fixes the Statutory Minimum Price (SMP) of sugarcane payable by
sugar factories for each sugar season (October - September). The Central Government has fixed 
the SMP for 2002-03 sugar season at Rs.64.50 per quintal linked to a basic recovery level of 
8.5%, subject to premium of 76 paise for every 0.1% point increase in recovery above that level.
2. State Governments have no power to fix prices of sugarcane.

records.title: LOANS OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO DABHOL POWER PROJECT .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Dabhol Power Project was started with the loans 
advanced by the financial institutions of the country;
(b) if so, the total amount spent so far by these institutions on the maintenance and 
running, along with the cost of construction of the project; and
(c) the percentage of the said amount of the total expenditure made thereon?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )
(a) : The Dabhol power project was constructed using a mix of equity and loan 
funds. The equity was brought in by the sponsors viz. Enron, General Electric, Bechtel 
and the Maharashtra Power Development Corporation Limited (MPDCL). The loan 
funds were advanced by a consortium of off-shore banks and Indian Financial 
Institutions/Banks (IFIs).
(b) & (c) : The exposure of the IFIs as on date aggregates Rs.6551 crores (Rs.3292 
crores by way of fund based assistance and Rs.3259 crores by way of guarantees). 
Phase-I of the project had commenced commercial operations in May, 1999, while Phase-
II was under construction. Phase-II of the project was complete to the extent of around 
92% as on 31.5.2001. Due to certain commercial disputes between Dabhol Power 
Company (DPC) and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), MSEB stopped 
taking power from Phase-I from 29th May, 2001 and construction of Phase-II was 
suspended due to termination of construction contracts on 17th June, 2001. From June, 
2001 onwards, the expenditure on asset preservation, security and payment of insurance 
premia, was being incurred out of funds available in the accounts of DPC. From 
September, 2002 onwards, after depletion of funds in the accounts of DPC, the principal 
IFIs have been incurring this expenditure. As on December 2, 2002, IFIs have incurred 
an expenditure of Rs.7.26 crores for asset preservation, security and insurance premia.

records.title: (clubbed) INDIA S PETITION AGAINST HUGE SUBSIDY PROVIDED BY USA H
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has filed petition in the WTO against the huge subsidy
 being provided by the USA;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the issues objected to by India; and
(c) by when a decision in the matter is likely to be taken by the WTO?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a) to (c): No, Sir. However, Brazil has sought consultations with the USA regarding subsidies
being given by it to upland cotton. In accordance with the provisions of the Understanding on
Rules and Procedures Governing the Settlement of Disputes (DSU) of the World Trade Organization (WTO), India has notified the consulting countries of it`s desire to be joined in the consultations as a third party. Further action will be taken in accordance with the provisions of the DSU. 
Besides, in the context of the on-going negotiations in agriculture under the Doha Work 
Programme of the WTO, India has proposed substantial reductions in all trade-distorting 
domestic support and the elimination of export subsidies by developed countries. 
The negotiations are scheduled to conclude by 1 January 2005.

records.title: EMPLOYMENT OF RETIRED RAILWAY EMPLOYEES IN COMMERCIAL INSTITUTIONS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of retired railway
 employees are employed with commercial institutions,
 contracting with the Railways ;
(b) if, so the details thereof and the posts held by each of
 them formerly ;
(c) whether it is also a fact that they give undue benefits to
 the private enterprises because of their earlier knowledge
 and acquaintance and affect the working of the Railways ;
 and
(d) if so, Government’s reaction thereto and the steps taken to
 check the same?
 ANSWER

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA)
(a) to (d) : Only Group ‘A’ officers are required to
seek prior permission from the Government for getting
employed with a private firm during the first two years
following retirement and Group ‘B’ officers are required
to inform the Railway in such cases. Apart from this,
there is no restriction or condition in the retired
Railway employees accepting commercial employment with
firms including those contracting with the Railways.
Therefore, it is not possible to maintain information
regarding all such employees employed with commercial
institutions. In view of this, it is also not possible
to have a feed back on such retired employees giving
undue benefit, if any, to others.

records.title: GROWTH RATE FOR TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are apprehensions over the present role of the State 
Governments in achieving the annual growth rate of eight per cent during Tenth 
Five Year Plan;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether those States have been identified in which the accomplishment of the 
above mentioned growth rate target is getting to be very difficult; if so, the names 
of such States?

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC 
ENERGY AND SPACE 
(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)
(a) to (c) : The Approach Paper to the Tenth Five Year Plan as approved by the National 
Development Council (NDC) envisages an annual average growth target of 8 per cent for 
the nation. A commitment has also been made in the Approach Paper to break up the 
growth target State-wise, taking into account the potentials and constraints of each State, 
since it is not necessary for each State to grow individually at an annual average rate of 8 
per cent in order to make the national growth target achievable. The Tenth Five Year 
Plan (2002-07), which would contain the State-wise growth target, is yet to be approved 
by the National Development Council.

records.title: SCHOOLS FOR PRIMARY EDUCATION .
details:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn towards the
fact that according to the Planning Commission the number of
non-school going children in the age group of 6 to 14 years is
80 million;
(b) if so, whether Government confirms this figure;
(c) if not, the assessment of Government in this regard; and
(d) the number of schools or classes required to be
introduced in the country for such children?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(PROF. RITA VERMA)
(a) to (d): According to the Draft Approach Paper to the Tenth
Five Year Plan (2002-2007) circulated by the Planning
Commission in May, 2001, it was stated that out of
approximately 200 million children in the age group 6-14 years
only 120 million are in schools. However, as per the latest
figures available in the Selected Educational Statistics,
brought out by this Ministry for the year 2000-01, out of the
projected child population of 19.2 crores in the age-group 6-
14, 15.7 crores have been enrolled in schools.
According to an estimate prepared by the Government under
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), there would be a requirement of
11.35 lakh additional class rooms in the next 10 years for 100%
enrolment (allowing for a class room for every teacher in
primary/upper primary schools and a room for the Head Master in
upper primary school).

records.title: FERTILIZER POLICY .
details:
(a) whether Government have declared a long term policy for chemical fertilizers, 
which would be brought into force from the next financial year; 
(b) if not, the facts in this regard; and 
(c) the salient features of this policy as a result of which the interest of the consumers, 
manufacturers and traders is likely to be protected to greater extent?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)
(a) to (c): The new pricing policy for urea units, being formulated keeping in view the 
recommendations of Expenditure Reforms Commission, is proposed to be introduced w.e.f. 
1.4.2003 and will replace the existing Retention Price Scheme. The new policy will be in 
the shape of Group Concession Scheme, which will aim at greater transparency, uniformity 
and efficiency in subsidy disbursements to urea manufacturing units and will induce urea 
manufacturers to take cost reduction measures on their own and be competitive. The 
farmers would continue to get urea at statutorily notified Maximum Retail Price.

(a) to (b) Yes, Sir. NALCO is a public sector industrial undertaking. It was established on 7th January in the year 1981 and commissioned in 1987.
