records.title: GAP BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND EXPORT OF TEXTILES .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that 15 per cent of the total production of the country is produced under the textile industry while its share in the overall export is 30 per cent.
(b) if not, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether there is need to increase production to reduce the gap between production and export; and
(d) if so, Government`s reaction thereon ?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES 
(SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR)
(a) & (b) The textile sector contributes about 14% to the industrial production and about 35% of exports of the country.
(c) &(d) The Government has been taking several steps from time to time to increase production and productivity of textile sector. Some of the important initiatives are as under: -
1) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUF) has been made operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and Upgradation of this sector.
2) Government has recently launched Technology Mission for Cotton. One of the important ingredients of the Mission is to improve cotton processing facilities by upgrading/modernising the existing ginning and pressing factories.
3) Allowing foreign equity participation upto 100%, through automatic route, in the textile sector with certain exceptions.
4) The facility to import capital goods under Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme at 5% concessional rate of duty.
5) The woven segment of ready-made garments has been de-reserved from SSI Sector.
6) To prepare and sensitise our textile and garment industry to conform to the ecological requirements of importing countries by providing facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories.
7) National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its six branches and Apparel Training & Design Centres (ATDCs) are running various courses/ programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements of textile industry in the field of design, merchandising and marketing.
8) The New Exporters` Entitlement (Quota) Policies announced for the period 2000-2004 to provide stability and continuity and encourage competitiveness in textile exports. 
9) The National Textile Policy 2000 has recently been announced to provide the policy direction for orderly and sustained development and growth of the textile industry in a harmonious way and to give a thrust to textile exports.
Besides the above, a comprehensive package for the textile industry has been announced in the Union Budget (2001-02) proposals, which include:-
- A provision for introduction of a new `Apparel Park Scheme.
- Excise duty on textile items has been rationalised to a single rate of 16% CENVAT. However, cotton yarn including sewing thread would continue at the effective rate of 8% duty.
- Reduction in customs duty from 15% to 5% on 159 specified textile and garment machineries. 
- 10% surcharge on imports has been withdrawn.
- Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered under TUFS, have been extended the facility of accelerated depreciation at the rate of 50%.

details:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS AND SHIPPING 
(SHRI ARUN JAITLEY) 
.SP2 
(a)&(b) The delay in hearing of cases in courts is due to
various complex factors. These include vacant posts of
judges, frequent adjournments, lawyers, strike etc.
(c)&(d) Various steps have been taken by the Government and
the Judiciary to speed up the disposal of cases such as
filling up of vacancies of judges, simplification of rules and
procedures on the basis of the advice and recommendations of
expert bodies, like the Law Commission, the Malimath Committee
etc. 
The Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act 1999,
inter alia, stipulates that adjournments shall not be granted
more than three times to a party during the hearing of the
suit. The relevant amendments are awaiting notification.

records.title: UTILISATION OF WATER RIVER BASIN .
details:
(a) whether any assessment has been made by Government
 about the quantity of water available from rivers of the
 Ganga basin;
(b) if so, the quantity of water flowing annually in the
rivers of this basin alongwith the names of the same;
(c) the assessment regarding the quantity of water that can
be utilised from each river; and
(d) the quantity of water being used from each river at
present?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY) 
(a) to (d) Yes Sir. The mean annual run off in river
Ganga in India is estimated to be 501.6 Billion Cubic Metres 
(BCM). Some of the major tributaries of river Ganga are
Ramganga, Yamuna, Tons, Gomati, Ghagra, Son, Gandak, Kosi
and Mahananda. An assessment of the quantity of Water that
can be utilised and the quantity that is being utilised has
not been made separately for each tributary of Ganga. For
the basin as whole, the quantity of water that can be
utilised annually is estimated to tbe 250 BCM. During the
year 2000, the utilisation was estimated to be 150.8 BCM for
irrigatio; 7.9 BCM for domestic use and 5.9 BCM for
industrial use.

records.title: HARVESTING OF RAIN WATER .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been average rain fall in
 the monsoon seasons in the country during the last three years;
(b) if so, the quantity of water being available through the rain
fall in the country;
(c) whether Government have made any assessment with regard to the
harvesting of this rain water; and
(d) if so, the estimated quantity of such harvested rain water out
of the total rain water?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY) 
(a) Yes Sir, the South-West monsoon rainfall is defined as
‘Normal’ when the rainfall received in the country as a whole is
within 90% to 110% of the long term average. In the years 1998,
1999 and 2000 the rainfall in South West monsoon was 105%, 96% and
92% respectively of the long term average. 
(b),(c) & (d) India receives an average annual precipitation of
4000 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM) which includes rainfall and snow.
Out of this, 3,000 BCM occurs during monsoon. The average annual
flow in various rivers of the country is assessed at 1869 BCM. Out
of this, utilizable flow by conventional methods is estimated at
690 BCM. In addition, about 200 to 250 BCM can be utilized through
interbasin water transfer from the surplus river basins to the
deficit river basins.
A live storage capacity of 177 BCM has been created
by construction of large dams and medium projects upto 1995.
Projects to add an additional capacity of about 75 BCM are under
construction and 132 BCM are under planning. It has also been
estimated that about 24 BCM of rainwater is stored in 3.5 lakh
minor irrigation tanks. Further, 432 BCM of ground water is
replenishable out of which 154 BCM is being used.
Government of India is also promoting rainwater
harvesting through Watershed Management Program, Artificial
recharge of ground water and rooftop rainwater harvesting under
various schemes. An assessment of the total quantity of rainwater
harvested through these means is not made.

records.title: DISINVESTMENT OF PUBLIC SECTOR INDUSTRIAL INSTITUTIONS
details:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)
(a) Disinvestment of the Government equity in the Central Public Sector Enterprises is being carried out in accordance with the disinvestment policy of the Government as enunciated from time to time. Its main elements are:
· Restructuring and reviving potentially viable PSUs;
· Closing down PSUs, which cannot be revived;
· Bringing down Government equity in all non-strategic PSUs to 26% or lower, if necessary; and
· Fully protect the interests of workers
It has also been decided that the Strategic Public Sector Enterprises would be those in the areas of:
1) Arms and ammunitions and the allied items of defence equipment, defence air-crafts and warships
2) Atomic energy (except in the areas related to the generation of nuclear power and applications of radiation and radio-isotopes to agriculture medicine and non-strategic industries) 
3) Railway transport
Moreover, for the non-strategic Public Sector Enterprises, the reduction of Government share to 26% would not be automatic and the manner and pace of doing so would be worked out on a case to case basis. A decision in regard to the percentage of disinvestment i.e., Government share going down to less than 51% or to 26%, would be taken on the following considerations: 
(i) Whether the Industrial sector requires the presence of the public sector as a countervailing force to prevent concentration of power in private hands, and 
(ii) Whether the Industrial sector requires a proper regulatory mechanism to protect the consumer interests before Public Sector Enterprises are privatised.
No separate scheme has been formulated to disinvest all public sector industrial units. 
(b) & (c ) Do not arise in view of a above. 
(e) The realization from disinvestment of equity depends on various factors like market conditions, financial performance of the company, terms and conditions of sale, interest of the investor(s) / buyer (s), advise of the professional consultants etc. No estimates of amounts likely to accrue from disinvestment can, therefore, be made.

records.title: REFORMS IN TECHNICAL EDUCATION .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a need for
comprehensive reform in technical education in the
country;
(b) if so, whether Government have prepared any draft
scheme for the said reforms; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and what decision has
been taken by Government for getting assistance from
private sector to implement this scheme?

THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)
(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the Table of the
House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE REPLY TO
THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.56 (H) FOR 23.02.2001
ASKED BY SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND DR. D.MASTHAN REGARDING
REFORMS IN TECHNICAL EDUCATION
`Reforms in technical education in the country is a
continuous process and this is achieved through the
implementation of the National Policy on Education (NPE)
and the Programme of Action (PoA). It includes
coordinated and planned development of technical
education as embodied in the All India Council for
Technical Education Act, 1987. For the development of
technical education, AICTE runs several schemes such as
Modernisation and Removal of Obsolescence, Thrust Area
Programme in Technical Education, Research and
Development Programme, Entrepreneurship and Management
Development Programme, Early Faculty Induction Programme,
Quality Improvement Programme, strengthening of National
Board of Accreditation, etc. An All India Board of IT
Education has also been constituted under AICTE.
Apart from the initiatives on the part of the AICTE,
recent initiatives taken to strengthen the technical
education system include strengthening and consolidation
of infrastrcutural facilities in Indian Institutes of
Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management 
(IIMs), Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Regional
Engineering Colleges (RECs) etc; establishment of more
IITs, IIMs and Engineering Colleges; establishment of
Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIIT) at
Allahabad and Indian Institute of Information Technology
& Management (IIITM) at Gwalior; National Programme for
HRD in IT, Review of Postgraduate Education; increase of
students intake in engineering and technical
institutions; increasing output of information technology
manpower; mobilization of private initiatives;
development of technologies in emerging areas and their
transfer to user agencies through technology development
missions; transfer of techno-economic advances in
technical education and appropriate technologies to rural
people through expansion of Community Polytechnics;
Scheme for upgrading existing polytechnics to integrate
the physically disabled in the main stream of technical
and vocational education; modernization of institutions
and development of R&D base; Technician Education
Project; modernization of libraries and switch over to
electronic libraries with interconnectivity; etc. RECs
are being strengthened as per the Mashelkar Committee
recommendations to become world class institutions 
(Centres of Excellence). Furthermore, technical
education system will also work for improving the
productivity of the informal sector of the economy.
Private Sector is involved substantially in running
of technical institutes, some of which are of very good
quality, under the overall supervision of AICTE. `

records.title: PRICE REVISION OF CHEMICAL FERTILIZERS .
details:
(a) whether Government are considering to revise the prices of chemical fertilizers in the 
country ;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor ; and 
(c) what percentage of profit is fixed for producers while fixing fertilizer prices, at present?

MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA)
______________________________________________________________________________
(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement referred to in reply to the parts (a) to (c) of Rajya Sabha Starred 
Question No. 382 to be answered on 15.12.2000. 
(a) and (b): Government fixes the farm gate price of urea and gives maximum 
indicative price for DAP, MOP and complex fertilizers. No revision of these prices is 
envisaged at this juncture. 
(c): Producers of indigenous urea and DAP/complex fertilizers get 
subsidy/concessions to bridge the gap between the selling price at which they are 
required to sell and their cost of production depending on the calculations made under 
Retention Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme in case of urea and the Concession Scheme in 
operation for DAP/complex fertilizers. A 12% post-tax return on net worth is built into 
the RPS. Similarly in the case of indigenous DAP, 12% post-tax return on net worth is 
envisaged while determining the cost of production under the Concession Scheme. For 
complex grade fertilizers and SSP, the rate of concession is determined taking into 
account their nutrient content and the concession on per unit of nutrients in indigenous 
DAP and MOP.

records.title: FLOW OF WASTE MATERIALS IN GANGA AND YAMUNA .
details:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS 
(SHRI T.R. BAALU)
(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. According to the survey conducted by Central Pollution Control Board, the waste water of the cities and towns is flowing into the waters of Ganga and Yamuna rivers at many places. The estimated quantity of wastewater discharged into these rivers is about 5300 million liters per day. 
(c) The percentage of wastewater over the total fresh water flowing into these rivers is not estimated as it varies on day to day basis. However, both the rivers suffer for want of minimum flow needed to maintain the desired river regime. For example, in Yamuna river in its stretch from Tajewala to Etawah, there is no perennial flow during non-monsoon months of the year and what is seen flowing in the river particularly in Delhi is the wastewater of the city discharged in partly treated and partly untreated condition. Similarly, the river Ganga has low flow conditions from Hardwar downstream to Varanasi.

details: SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND RURAL AND AGRO INDUSTR

THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES
(SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)
(a): Yes, Sir.
(b): No separate target is fixed for lending to Small Scale Industries (SSIs) for loans to be advanced by Indian banks. Advances to SSIs are included in the overall target of 40% under priority sector to be achieved by banks. However, in order to ensure that banks do not ignore the credit needs of smaller units among SSIs, it has been stipulated that banks should lend at least 40% of their advances to SSI sector to those units whose investment in plant and machinery is upto Rs. 5 lakh and 20% to those units whose investment in plant and machinery is between Rs. 5 lakh and Rs. 25 lakh. The foreign banks in India have been given by the Reserve Bank of India a target of 10% of net bank credit to be achieved by them for loans to SSIs. As at the end of March 2000, they have achieved the target and the percentage stood at 10.23.
(c): No, Sir.
(d): Does not arise.
(e): As per the Reserve Bank of India, as on 31st March, 2000, public sector banks net credit to Small Scale Sector was 15.63% of their total net bank credit.

records.title: IMROVEMENT IN THE TRANSMISSION SYSTEM .
details:
(a) whether after bringing about an improvement in transmission system, 
Government have connected each of the 250 MW power generating projects in such a 
manner, so that the generated power can easily be transmitted in those areas of the 
country facing power shortage at the time of requirement;
(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and
(c) if not, whether it is also a fact that in the absence of adequate transmission system 
power production has to be stopped sometimes in the project?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA)
(a) to (c): The power system in the country has been developed on regional basis 
comprising of Northern, Western, Southern, Eastern and North-Eastern Regional Grids. 
The transmission system for evacuation and utilization of power from generating units 
including 250 MW units are planned for utilization in a regional grid system in which the 
generating unit is located.
 At present Eastern and North Eastern Regions are operating in 
synchronism and it is proposed to interconnect Northern, Eastern and North Eastern 
Regions by the end of the 10th Plan and to interconnect all the regions and operate them 
as a National Grid by the end of the 11th Plan.
 At present, POWERGRID has a capacity to transfer 4350 MW of power 
on inter-regional basis, which is likely to increase to 14,000 MW by the end of 2007 and 
30,000 MW by 2012.
 On account of low load development in the constituent states of Eastern 
Regional system, certain power stations have to be operated at lower PLF. Efforts are 
being made to transfer surplus power from this region to the adjoining regions and on the 
basis of existing inter regional system about 1000 MW power is being transferred at 
present to the adjoining regions. This capacity would increase further with the 
commissioning of 400 KV Biharshariff to Allahabad Line in 2001.

records.title: ABOLITION OF GOVERNMENT MONOPOLY IN PETROLEUM SECTOR .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI E. PONNUSWAMY)
(a) to (e): Government in November 1997, decided the details of phasing of dismantling programme of administered pricing mechanism (APM) for moving towards a competitive market in the petroleum sector. Accordingly, the petroleum sector is scheduled for full deregulation from April 2002 onwards. Pursuant to the said decision, the consumer prices of all petroleum products except petrol, diesel, ATF, kerosene for public distribution system and domestic LPG have been decontrolled and the retention pricing system has been abolished for the refineries with effect from 1.4.1998. As per the programme, the price of domestic LPG is to be suitably adjusted to reach subsidy level at 15% of import parity during the year 2000-01. Suitable adjustment in prices of kerosene for public distribution would be made to reach subsidy level at 33.33% of the import parity. On full deregulation, 2002 onwards, the subsidy on kerosene for public distribution and LPG domestic will be transferred to the fiscal budget of the Government. The domestic consumer prices would depend on the oil and product prices in the international market.

records.title: EFFECT OF IMPORT ON INDIGENOUS TRADE
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
( SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH )
(a) to (c ) India has been following a consistent policy for gradual removal of restrictions on imports since 1991. Tariff line- wise import policy was first announced on 31.3.1996. As on that date, import of 6161tariff lines (at 10 digit level) out of the total number of 10202 was free. Import restrictions on 488 tariff lines were removed during the period 1.4.96 to 31.3.97. Further 391 tariff lines (at 8 digit level) were freed during the period 1.4.97 to 13.4.98 and 894 tariff lines (at 8 digit level) were freed on 1.4.99. Import restrictions on 714 tariff lines were removed on 31.3.2000. The removal of restriction as carried out on 31.03.2000 was a part of the consistent policy being followed since 1991.
The rate of growth in import of country`s non-petroleum non-gold items has not shown any significant increase. It was 6.88% in 1997-98, 4.04% in 1998-99, 5.47% in 1999-2000. These imports have shown a negative growth of 1.85% during the period April-Sept., 2000-2001. Nevertheless, significant increase has been noticed in the import of certain consumer goods such as umbrellas, locks, writing instruments, battery cells, toys, footwear etc. The Government is closely monitoring the situation and appropriate measures as necessary are being taken. Some of the measures taken recently include:
(i) Import duties on a number of items have been increased, for example, the duty on arecanut has been raised from 35% to 100%, on poultry products from 35% to 100%, on wheat from 0% to 50%, on skimmed milk powder from 0% to 60%, on apple from 35% to 50%, and on rice from 0% to 80%. 
(ii) Suo-moto anti-dumping investigations have been initiated in respect of import of battery cells, battery operated toys and sports shoes. 
(iii) Import of all packaged commodities have been made subject to compliance of all the conditions of the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodity ) Order, 1977, as applicable on domestic producers. 
(iv) Import of 131 products has been made subject to compliance of the mandatory Indian quality standards as applicable to domestic goods. For compliance of this requirement all manufacturers/ exporters of these products to India shall be required to register themselves with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). The list of 131 products includes various food preservatives and additives, milk powder, infant milk food, certain kinds of cement, household and similar electrical appliances, gas cylinders and multipurpose dry batteries.
Since, the situation is being closely monitored and necessary action as warranted ia being taken, there is no proposal to issue a White Paper on the subject for the present.

records.title: SUBSIDY ON FERTILIZERS
details:
MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA)
______________________________________________________________________________
(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO.182 BY DR.D.MASTHAN AND SHRI KAPIL SIBAL TO BE 
ANSWERED ON 1.12.2000
(a) to (d) : The Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC), in its 2nd Report Part-I, submitted in 
September 2000 has recommended rationalisation of fertilizer subsidies and dismantling of the 
controlled system in a phased manner. It has further recommended that the existing Retention 
Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme needs to be replaced by an easily enforceable system that provides 
incentives to the manufacturers to be cost efficient and ensures a desired level of self sufficiency 
with minimal support from the Government.
 The Report of the ERC is under examination by the Department of Fertilizers and inter-
ministerial consultation will be held soon to finalise the views of the Government on the 
recommendation of the ERC.
 However, the issues pertaining to reassessment of capacities of urea manufacturing units, 
also referred to in the ERC Report, have been referred to a Committee headed by Dr. Y.K. 
Alagh for suitable advice and recommendation.
 The Government has meanwhile taken corrective action by undertaking interim 
reassessment of capacity of high capacity utilisation urea units w.e.f. 1.4.2000 which would 
reduce the subsidy outgo by approximately Rs. 450 crore per annum under the existing Retention 
Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme.
 The Government is in the process of formulating a new pricing policy, to replace the 
existing Retention Price -cum-Subsidy Scheme, keeping in view the recommendations made by 
the High Powered Committee headed by Prof. C.H. Hanumantha Rao and the Expenditure 
Reforms Commission headed by Shri K.P. Geethakrishnan.

records.title: AMOUNT FOR MAINTENANCE OF GREENERY .
details:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI T.R.BAALU)
(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Environment & Forests have formulated National Forestry Action Programme (NFAP), a comprehensive strategic plan for the next twenty years to increase the forest cover in the country to the desired 33% as mandated in the National Forest Policy, 1988. It is estimated that Rs.133903 crores would be required in the next twenty years for implementation of National Forestry Action Programme. The requirement for first year of the Plan is Rs. 4669 crores. 
(c) The various components of National Forestry Action Programme are as follows:- 
1. Protection of Existing Forest Resources: It has three main-sub programmes. 
(i) Forest protection, 
(ii) Soil and water conservation, and 
(iii) Protected areas and biodiversity conservation. 
2. Improvement of Forest Productivity: It has four main sub-programmes. 
(i) Rehabilitation of degraded forests, 
(ii) Research and technology development, 
(iii) Development of Non Wood Forest Products and 
(iv) Assisting private initiatives with community participation. 
3. Reduction of Total Demand: It has three main sub programmes for the efficient uses of 
(i) Fuelwood and fodder, 
(ii) Timber 
(iii) Non Wood Forest Products. 
4. Strengthening of Policy and Institutional Framework: It has three main sub-programmes. 
(i) Central forestry administration, 
(ii) Central forestry institutions, and 
(iii) State forestry administration and institutions. 
5. Expanding Forest Area: It has two main sub-programmes. (I) Tree plantation on forest and non-forest lands, and 
(ii) People`s participation in plantations and its protection.

records.title: PRODUCTION OF TRANSGENIC COTTON
details:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
( PROF. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI )
(a), (b),(c) and (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 446 TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.08.2000-REGARDING PRODUCTION
OF TRANSGENIC COTTON.____
Contained limited field experiments on transgenic cotton were carried out in various regions of the country.
These experiments were not for production of transgenic cotton but were for evaluation of transgenic characters
in cotton plants i.e. the effect of an introduced transgene that codes for a protein (Bt protein), produced by
Bacillus thuringiensis, a bacterium commonly occurring in nature. During 1998-2000, evaluation of agronomic
performance and on-farm trials for transgenic cotton to ascertain the yield, morphological characteristics,
persistence, germination rate and pest load were carried out by the scientists of M/s. Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds
Co. Ltd. (MAHYCO), Mumbai in private lands and State Agricultural Universities in the State of Andhra Pradesh,
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. The institutes were Acharya NG
Ranga Agricultural University, Rajendra Nagar, at its Regional Research Station, Lamb, Guntur, as well as at
Warangal in Andhra Pradesh; Punjab Rao Krishi Vidyapeeth at Akola; and Marathwada Agricultural University,
Parbhani in Maharashtra. The effect of Bt cottonseeds on goats as model was studied at the Indian Toxicological
Research Centre (ITRC), Lucknow and Bt protein was not found to be toxic. The agro-scientists of MAHYCO had
conducted detailed post-harvest observations on the impact of Bt cotton cultivars at Jalna in Maharashtra;
Dharwad in Karnataka; Hyderabad in Andhra Pradesh and Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. A team of over 20 scientists of
R & D laboratory of MAHYCO led by Dr. Usha Zehr, Dr. S. K. Mukherjee and others conducted these experiments. It
was concluded from these studies that there was significant increase in the yield from transgenic plants. There
was also noticeable reduction in the spraying of chemical pesticides for bollworms, a major pest of cotton. The
residues of Bt protein in soil were either non-existent or were extremely low and did not have any effect on the
microbial populations of the soil samples. The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee has approved on 30th June
2000, large scale field trials with scientific monitoring in some States. Work has started in the States of
Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

records.title: REDUCTION OF ECONOMIC COST OF FCI .
details:
(a) whether the Government have sought suggestions during last three years to reduce the
 economic cost of Food Corporation of India; 
(b) if so, the names of institutions alongwith the suggestions given by them to the 
Government; and
(c) the action taken by the Government to implement those suggestions?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI SRIRAM CHAUHAN )
(a),(b) & (c): The Administrative Staff College of India, Hyderabad has been engaged to 
study the cost of acquisition and distribution of wheat and rice by the Food Corporation of 
India so as to arrive at ways and means to reduce its Economic Cost of wheat and rice. The
final report of the College is expected by the end of September, 2000 only.
 However, in the meanwhile the Expenditure Reforms Commission which was set up by the 
Government of India in February, 2000 has re-viewed the methodology of allocation of 
distribution cost between stocks maintained by the Food Corporation of India for distribution
through Public Distribution System and buffer stocks. The Commission has made three important
changes in the methodology. 
(i) At present, only, the annual accretion to the buffer stocks is reckoned for 
allocation of distribution cost. However, considering that it would be necessary for Government
to rotate the stocks held as buffer stocks over a two to three year period in the interest of
maintaining quality, the Commission has recommended that transport cost and transit losses to 
the extent of one-third of the opening stocks of buffer be charged to the buffer carrying cost. 
(ii) The Commission has felt that carry-over charges, namely, charges paid to the State
agencies involved in the procurement of wheat beyond 30th June every year, should be part of 
the buffer carrying cost rather than economic cost of wheat for public distribution.
(iii) The Commission has also recommended that the economic cost should be estimated on the 
basis of pooling of opening stocks available with the Food Corporation of India in the beginning
of the year and stocks procured during the current year, rather than being based on the minimum
support price of the current year. 
On account of these changes in the methodology, which have been accepted by Government, the 
economic cost of wheat and rice for public distribution have been revised to Rs.830 per quintal 
for wheat instead of Rs.900 per quintal as before and to Rs.1,130 per quintal for rice instead 
of Rs.1,180 per quintal as originally estimated.

records.title: EXTENT OF COMMUNICATION FACILITIES IN THE RURAL AREAS VIS VIS URBAN AREAS
details:
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.402 FOR 22ND AUGUST, 2000 REGARDING EXTENT OF COMMUNICATION FACILITIES IN RURAL AREAS VIS-À-VIS URBAN AREAS
1. Although it is a fact that the urban telephone connections are higher as compared to rural areas, this is mainly due to the fact that earlier the demand for telephones was less in rural areas. However, now the demand for rural areas is also coming up and Department is making all out efforts to cope up with the demand of the rural areas. 
2. The telecom facilities in rural areas have progressed considerably over the last few years. Presently, Department of Telecom Operations is operating 2,74,20,192 Direct Exchange Lines (DELs) in the country out of which 49,26,287 DELs are working in rural areas. This is being done through 28,204 telephone exchanges in the country out of which 21,879 are in rural areas. In addition, out of 6.07 lakh villages, Public Telephones have been provided in 3,76,886 villages. It is further planned to provide a total of 57.9 lakh lines in the country (including MTNL) in the current financial year 2000-2001, out of which 14.2 lakh lines will be in rural areas through the existing exchanges in rural areas as well as 3,431 new exchanges planned for opening in rural areas. It is also planned to provide 19 lakh lines in rural areas during 2001-2002. 
3. The Government has decided as a policy, to make available Telephone on Demand by the end of Ninth Five Year Plan in the entire country which includes both rural as well as urban areas along with the contribution of private sector. The Government has also envisaged that all the exchanges in the country will be covered with reliable transmission media by the end of Ninth Plan. The New Telecom Policy - 1999 also envisages that each village in the country will have at least one Public Telephone by the end of Ninth Five Year Plan along with the contribution from Private Sector. All out efforts are being made to achieve these targets.

records.title: JOINT FOREST MANAGEMENT PROGRAMME
details:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMNET AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. BAALU)
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) and (c): In accordance with the provisions of the National Forest Policy,1988, Government of India had issued guidelines to all the state governments on June 1, 1990 for involving village communities in the regeneration and protection of degraded forest lands under the Joint Forest Management (JFM) Programme. After a review of the JFM activities, the Central Government have issued fresh guidelines on 21st February 2000 to further strengthen the JFM programme in the country. No specific targets have been fixed for the programme, as it is a continuing and evolving process. The programme has picked up quite well during the last 10 years and as reported by various State Governments as on 1.1.2000, 10.249 million hectare of forests area is being managed in collaboration with 36,130 JFM Committees in 22 states. Central Government have requested the State Governments to involve the JFM Committees in all the afforestation programmes. Under the Centrally sponsored schemes of the Ministry, an amount of Rs.477.50 crore has been earmarked during the ninth plan period on afforestation activities and JFM is an integral component in the implementation of these schemes.

land;
(b) if so, the unused land available at present with
railways;
(c): the area of such land which can be developed as
commercial area and income can be earned therefrom; and
(d): the names of such cities where such land is available,
alongwith the area thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)
(a): In view of the declining budgetary support from the
General Exchequer in the last decade or so, Railways have
decided to utilise air-space over its identified vacant
land/stations requiring re-building.
(b): About 0.25 lakh Hectare .

vacant plots in Mumbai, Delhi, Calcutta, Chennai, Bangalore
and Hyderabad in the First Phase, with the intention to
extend commercial development of railway land/air-space to
all other parts of the country in phases and after
gaining experience. The commercial potential of each site
varies widely from place to place and from location to
location. As the endeavour is going to continue for a long
time, it is difficult to assess the total income out of
this venture.

details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)
(a) It is a fact that the production of pulses is less than the demand of pulses in the country, because of several constraints like cultivation by small and marginal farmers, on marginal lands and under rainfed conditions.
 The production and consumption of pulses in the country during the last 3 years is given below:
Year Production (Lakh Tonnes) Consumption (Lakh Tonnes) 
1996-97 142.44 148.60 
1997-98 129.80 133.60 
1998-99 148.09 148.90 
(b) To make the country self sufficient in the field of production of pulses, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme National Pulses Development Project (NPDP) is being implemented in the country for increasing the production and productivity of pulses.
(c)&(d) The Planning Commission has fixed a production target of pulses for the IX Plan i.e. 2001-2002 at 16.5 million tonnes to make the country self sufficient in pulses production. The Govt. of India is making all efforts to achieve the targetted production of pulses. For increasing the production of pulses a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Pulses Development Project (NPDP) is under implementation in 25 States/2 UTs. The scheme envisages financial assistance to the states for production and distribution of Certified Seeds, seed minikits, rhyzobium culture, sprinkler sets, improved farm implements etc. In addition, field demonstration and farmers training are also being organised for the transfer of improved production & protection technology to the farmer’s field for increasing the production of pulses.

records.title: NORMS FOR SELECTION OF COLONIES FOR REGULARISATION.
details:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION 
( SHRI JAGMOHAN )
(a)to(e): In early 1993, Govt. of National Capital Territory
of Delhi decided to recommend to the Government of India for
regularisation of unauthorised colonies in Delhi which had come
up before March 31, 1993. Soon thereafter, a public interest
writ petition was filed by the Common Cause in the Delhi High
Court against this proposal/recommendations. The High Court, in
its interim orders, stayed action or decision by the Government
for regularising these colonies.
On the directions of the Court, a High Powered Committee
headed by Secretary, Ministry of Urban Development was
constituted to go into the entire gamut of issue on unauthorised
colonies. On the basis of the report of this Committee, the
High Court asked the Government to submit its view to the Court
in respect of regularisation of the colonies and the terms and
conditions on which such regularisation could be done. After
consulting all the local authorities including the Government of
National Capital Territory of Delhi, a draft proposal was
prepared. This proposal was sent to Delhi Government and the
Government of Delhi conveyed its agreement to the draft proposal
in October, 1999. Thereafter, the Government of India
formulated its views and these views are being submitted to the
High Court through an affidavit. The High Court, after
considering these views and holding further proceedings in the
matter, will take appropriate decision. The Government will
take further action in accordance with the directions/orders of
the High Court.

(SHRI T.N.SHANMUGAM)
(a): Yes, Sir. The Coal Sector Rehabilitation
Project(CSRP) has been conceived to cater for investment
towards increasing coal production in the 24 sub-
project under five subsidiaries i.e. Central
coalfields Limited(CCL), Mahanadi Coalfields Limited 
(MCL), Western Coalfields Limited (WCL), South Eastern
Coalfields Limited (SECL) and Northern Coalfields
Limited(NCL) of Coal India Limited (CIL) .The main
objectives of the CSRP is to make CIL commercially
viable , self-sustaining and increase coal production
for meeting the future demand of the country.
(b): The total investment in the project is estimated
US$ 1.695 billion, out of which US $ 1.03 billion will be

for International Co-operation on 50:50 ratio. The
balance amount will be financed by the subsidiaries of
Coal India Limited i.e. CCL,MCL,WCL,SECL and NCL .
The project consists of an investment component,
technical assistance and training component. The
investment component is to finance procurement of Heavy
Earth Moving Machinery(HEMM) in 24 profitable mining sub-
projects and also construction of Coal handling
Plants(CHPs) in four of them. The technical assistance
-2-
component is envisaged to finance Coal India’s
institutional capacity development in the project
implementation , mining operations and management.
(c): The project was approved by the World Bank in
september,1997 and the loan became effective in June,1998
and disbursement for the project was started in
July,1998.

records.title: CONSENSUS ON THE DRAFT OF NATIONAL WATER POLICY .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that no consensus have been
 reached on the draft of National Water Policy;
(b) if so, the main reasons therefor; and
(c) what steps Government propose to take in this
direction?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY) 
(a) Yes Sir. 
(b)&(c) The draft of revised National Water Policy was
placed before the fourth meeting of the National Water
Resources Council under the Chairmanship of the Hon’ble
Prime Minister held on 7th July, 2000 for
consideration/adoption. The deliberations established a
broad consensus among the states on most of the issues
contained in the proposed policy, however, some of the areas
of differences were as under:-
i) Legislation for developing standardized national
information system.
ii) Establishing appropriate River Basin Organisations with
statutory powers.
iii) Water Allocation amongst States, and
iv) Amendment of Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956.
In order to achieve greater convergence and agreement on
these issues, the council has decided for constitution of a
Working Group of Ministers of all the States/UTs chaired by
Hon’ble Minister of Water Resources

records.title: NPAS OF BANKS .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALA SAHEB VIKHE PATIL)
(a)&(b): While gross NPAs of the public sector banks have gone up from Rs.51710 crore as on 31st March, 1999 to Rs.52593.52 crore (Provisional ) as on 31st March, 2000, in percentage term it has come down from 15.89% to 14.28% (Provisional) of gross advances. Net NPAs for the same period at Rs.24211.49 crore (8.13% of net advances) as on 31.3.1999 have gone up to Rs.25840.51 crore (8.20% of net advances) (provisional) as on 31.3.2000.
(c): The Banks take all possible steps to recover their dues from defaulters through various means such as close follow up, filing of suits etc. Also Government of India/Reserve Bank of India/Banks have taken several steps for recovery of bank dues which include framing and implementation of recovery policy by banks, filing of suits with Civil Courts, filing cases with Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs), strengthening and setting up more DRTs and DRATs compromise settlement through Settlement Advisory Committees and monitoring and follow up of non performing accounts. Reserve Bank of India have issued guidelines for recovery of bank dues in NPAs accounts up to Rs.5 crore which have been classified as doubtful/loss on a pre-determined cut-off date. Chief Executives of Public Sector Banks have been asked to personally monitor and follow-up recovery in higher value accounts in accordance with the policy laid down by the respective Boards.

THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)
(a) to (d): As per the provisional data on enrolment of classes I-XII
collected from Directorates of Education of all States/UTs for selected
education statistics. 1998-99, the percentage of drop out in School
Education (1998-99) in India is as follows:

( The dropout figures are calculated for I-XII by taking Class I enrolment
figure in a particular year and class XII enrolment after 11 years)
The drop-out data on higher levels of education is not collected by the
Department of Secondary Education & Higher Education.
The main reasons for drop-out at school level include:
- Social, economic and cultural factors;
- Inadequately provided school and insufficient teaching in schools;
- Perception of curriculum not being related to local needs;
- Indifference of parents towards education of children;
- Difficulties experienced by first generation learners; and
- Lack of community involvement in local schools.
The Department is making all efforts to reduce drop out rates by
establishing more schools, providing more teachers, improving quality

records.title: JOB PROSPECTS IN NEW INDUSTRIES
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there have been wide changes
 in the contribution of various sources in the gross
 domestic product of the country after adopting the policy
 of globalization and liberalisation;
(b) if so, whether the above changes have resulted in new
 job avenues in new industries whereas job opportunities in
 conventional industries have declined; and
(c) if so, the Government`s reaction in this regard?

MINISTER OF LABOUR 
(DR. SATYA NARAYAN JATIYA)
a), b) & c): A statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED
QUESTION NO. 61 BY SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND DR. D. MASTHAN
REGARDING JOB PROSPECTS IN NEW INDUSTRIES DUE FOR REPLY ON
27.7.2000.
Percentage distribution of Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
by economic activity at 1993-94 prices reveals an increasing
trend in respect of manufacturing; electricity, gas and
water supply; trade, hotel and restaurants; transport
storage and communication; financing, insurance, real estate
and business services; and community, social and personal
services. Decreasing trend has been observed in respect of
agriculture, forestry and fishing, and mining & quarrying.
There has been a steady increase in GDP in recent years
after adopting economic reforms.
Estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained
from the comprehensive surveys conducted by National Sample
Survey Organisation (NSSO). From the last two comprehensive
surveys on employment and unemployment conducted by NSSO
during 1987-88 and 1993-94 (latest available) a positive
annual growth rate of employment has been observed in all
the sectors of the economy. However, the annual growth rate
of employment was significant (more than 3.5 per cent p.a.)
in respect of electricity, gas and water Sapply; trade,
hotel and restaurants; transport, storage and communication.
financing, insurance, real estate and business services; and
community, social and personal services.
As per current trends, employment opportunities
particularly in manufacturing sector may not grow
significantly but at the same time new opportunities are
being created in the services sectors such as hotel &
restaurants, tourism, and information technology.

records.title: (clubbed) RED TAPISM AFFECTS ARMY PREPAREDNESS .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)
(a) to (c): The Defence Procurement Procedure was formulated and prescribed in 1992 by the Government. The procedure is comprehensive and includes measures to ensure that a conclusive and objective view is taken while selecting a weapon/weapon system and that extraneous factors do not influence the decision. The procedure is designed for procuring equipment against Qualitative Requirements specified, approved and confirmed by the user, through a system of trials and evaluation by the Services and through a process of competitive tendering to ensure cost advantages. Government is fully alive to the needs of the country`s defence preparedness and all steps are being taken to streamline the procurement process and to minimise the time taken in decision making. The Government have considered the comments made in certain quarters that Defence Procurement Procedures are coming in the way of time bound acquisition by the Armed Forces. In order to further streamline the procedure, a committee has been set up under Chairmanship of Vice Chief of Army Staff to examine the existing Defence Procurement Procedure in its entirety with a view to suggest specific measures for speedier processing of procurement cases.

 requirement?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
( SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY ) 
(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. 
(c) The State Governments formulate plans and take up
irrigation projects from their own plan allocations and as
per their own priorities. However, keeping in view the need
to cover additional areas under irrigation, the Government
of India has also taken/proposed to take various policy and
programme initiatives. These include revision of National
Water Policy, Command Area Development Programme,
preparation of National Perspectives for transfer of water
from surplus basins to water deficit areas, water management
practices, promoting efficient and economic use of water for
various purposes, artificial recharge of ground water,
emphasis on water conservation through various methods
including use of latest technologies and peoples’
participation in management of water for diverse uses.

details:
(a): whether it is a fact that various medicines in the country fall under the 
purview of Drug (Price Control) Order;
(b): if so, the total number of medicines which were under the purview of 
the said Order in March, 1997 and March, 2000, separately;
©: whether it is a fact that prices of medicines under the purview of Drug 
price control Order increased during the said period; if so, the percentage of 
the increase; and
(d): the percentage of increase in the prices of drugs which do not fall under 
the purview of the said Order?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS 
AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI RAMESH BAIS)
(a): Yes, Sir.
(b): In the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995, promulgated on 6.1.1995, 
76 bulk drugs were kept under price control as mentioned in the First 
Schedule of the said Order. However, two bulk drugs were omitted 
from the schedule in September, 1997 and presently 74 bulk drugs and 
formulations based thereon are under price control.
(c) and (d): Price fixation/revision of prices of drugs is an ongoing and 
continuous process. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, an 
attached office of the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals, have 
between the period August, 97 to March, 2000, fixed/revised price of 
965 formulation packs. Of the 965 packs, prices have been reduced for 
402 and raised for 408 packs. Prices for 124 packs were fixed for the 
first time, while no change was effected from the existing level in the 
case of 31 packs.

records.title: POWER GENERATION IN HYDRO AND THERMAL SECTORS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to revise 
 the existing ratio of power generation in hydro and thermal sectors 
 from 26:74 to 40:60 in the country;
(b) if so, by when the power generation as per the above average 
 is proposed to be started in the country;
(c) whether Government have made any assessment of benefits of 
 power production to be obtained as per the above average; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM )
(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 640 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 10.5.2000 REGARDING POWER 
GENERATION IN HYDRO AND THERMAL SECTORS.
(a) to (d) : Despite hydro-electric projects being recognised as the 
most economic and preferred source of electricity, share of hydro 
power has been declining steadily since 1963. The constraints which 
have affected hydro development are technical (difficult 
investigation, inadequacies in tunneling methods), financial 
(deficiencies in providing long term financing), tariff related issues 
and managerial weaknesses (poor contract management). The hydro 
projects are also affected by geological surprises (especially in the 
Himalayan region where underground tunneling is required), 
inaccessibility of the area, problems due to delay in land 
acquisition, and resettlement of project affected families, law and 
order problem in militant infested areas.
The Government had announced a Policy on Hydro Power 
Development in August, 1998 with the objective of accelerating the 
pace of hydro power development in the country. An improvement in the 
hydel-thermal mix is proposed to be achieved by 
(i) completion of the 
on-going hydro-electric projects 
(ii) initiating advance action for 
obtaining necessary approvals in respect of new hydro-electric 
projects for which Detailed Project Report (DPR) is available; and 
(iii) initiating work on survey and investigation in respect of new 
green field sites to enable preparation of DPR so that necessary 
approvals could be obtained and projects taken up for execution in a 
phased manner.
Advance action has been taken on fresh starts under 
Central Sector, as a result of which a number of new hydro projects 
have been approved namely Tuirial (60 MW) Mizoram; Chamera-II 
(300 MW) H.P.; Teesta-V (510 MW); Loktak Downstream (90 MW) Manipur; 
Koteshwar (400 MW) U.P.; Development of Projects in the Parbati Basin 
(2051 MW); and Dihang and Subansiri Basin (20700 MW). National 
Thermal Power Corporation has also entered into an agreement with 
Himachal Pradesh for execution of Kol Dam Project (800 MW). 
Simultaneously, advance action has been initiated on a number of other 
hydro electric projects namely Kameng (600 MW) Arunachal Pradesh; 
Tuivai (210 MW) Mizoram; Tipaimukh (1500 MW) Manipur; Lower Kopili 
(150 MW) Assam; Teesta Projects Stage-III, IV and VI (2055 MW) Sikkim; 
Pala Maneri (416 MW) U.P.; Lohari Nag (520 MW) U.P.; Rampur (800 MW) 
H.P., which will all yield capacity of more than 25,000 MW during the 
time frame of 11th Plan (2007-12) and beyond.
Efforts are also being made to arrive at a consensus 
amongst basin states regarding location of power projects locked up 
due to inter-state disputes, namely, Shivasamudram 270 MW, Mekedatu 
550 MW, Rasimanal 200 MW and Hogenakkal 120 MW in Cauvery basin. 
Similarly, Renuka Dam Project 60 MW and Kishau Multipurpose Project 
(600 MW) are also being pursued for an early execution.
Government is also committed to complete hydro-electric 
schemes languishing for a number of years for want of funds. An MOU 
with Government of U.P. has been signed recently in pursuance of which 
Government of U.P. will jointly execute Maneri Bhali Stage-II (304 MW) 
and Lakwar Vyasi (420 MW) with THDC and NHPC respectively.
A massive thrust is proposed to be given for hydro 
development by starting work on preparing DPRs in respect of hydro 
projects involving capacity of about 30000 MW in the next 5 years.

records.title: REPLACING PARTS MACHINERY IN POWER GENERATING UNITS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that power generation in the projects 
 can be increased by replacing plants/machinery in power generating 
 units in the country;
(b) whether Government have conducted any survey to replace 
 plants/machinery in the projects engaged in existing power generation; 
 and
(c) if so, the details thereof and total amount likely to be 
 spent thereon together with the annual increase in power generation?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER
( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )
(a) : Yes, Sir. It is fact that power generation in the 
projects can be increased by undertaking Renovation & Modernisation 
(R&M).
(b) & (c) : Government of India recognised the importance of R&M in 
1984 to improve the performance of old thermal generating units. 
Based on the performance analysis, 34 thermal power stations having 
163 units with a total installed capacity of 13570 MW were identified 
for carrying out R&M during 7th Plan period. A total amount of 
Rs. 1066 crores was incurred resulting into an additional generation 
of about 10,000 Million Units/Year. Subsequently, 44 thermal power 
stations having 198 generating units were identified under Phase-II 
programme during 8th Plan at an estimated cost of Rs. 2383 crores. 
The programme is at various stages of completion and on all-India 
basis, about 75% works have been completed resulting into an 
additional generation of 5000 Million Units per year after completion 
of partial works. Further, a large number of thermal units have 
completed/nearing completion their useful economic life and to keep 
these units in economical operation for another 15-20 years, many 
parts of the plants will need to be replaced under R&M/Life Extension 
programme.
Similarly, 55 hydel schemes with an aggregate installed 
capacity of 9653 MW were identified at an estimated cost of Rs. 1493 
crores to accure benefits of 2531 MW/7181 MUs.

records.title: TALKS WITH TERRORISTS .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)
(a),(b),(c) & (d): During his visit to Jammu and Kashmir on 26-27 July, 1997, the then Prime Minister had made an appeal to the misguided youth of the State, who have joined the militant ranks, to give up their guns, and said that the Government was prepared to have unconditional talks with them, to enable them to rejoin the mainstream. The Government is committed to the said offer of talks, within the constitutional frame work.
 The Prime Minister of India had spelt out the parameters for initiating a peace dialogue with militant outfits in the North East on 15 April, 1998 at Guwahati declaring :
 `To all those who have strayed from the paths of togetherness, whether in Assam or other States of the North East, I extend an invitation; come forward ; let us discuss, my Government is committed to holding talks, to a restoration of peace; let us do so within the four corners of our Constitution.`
Unstarred Question No. 3982 for 3.5.2000
Cease fire and peace talks with the NSCN(IM) are underway since 1 August, 1997. Suspension of operations with the Bodo Liberation Tiger (BLT) was also announced earlier this year. NSCN(K) have also issued a Press Release Offering a formal `cease fire` with the Government of India and political talks.
 The offer for talks have been made by the Government in view of its commitment to resolve all issues through negotiations. The Government are firmly of the view that violence has no place in a democratic polity and the people by and large want peace and an end to violence.

records.title: ANNUAL AVERAGE GROWTH RATE OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual production rate of agriculture was 3.1 per cent in 
the decade of 80`s has come down now to almost 2 per cent in 90`s; 
(b) if not, the assessment of Government in this regard; and 
(c) the reasons for this decline and the estimated rate likely to be gained in the first 
decade of 21st century?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OFAGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)
(a)&(b) The annual compound growth rates of agriculture production during the 
decade of 80`s and 90`s have been 3.72% and 2.21% per annum respectively.
(c) The deceleration in growth rate of production of agricultural crops taken as a group 
is mainly on account of deceleration in the rate of growth of yield rates.
The growth rate of production of agricultural crops depends upon a large number of 
factors such as agro-climatic conditions, performance of monsoon, timely application of 
seeds, fertilizers, managerial abilities of farmers, level of investment etc. Therefore, it is 
not possible to estimate at this stage, gain in growth rate in the first decade of 21st century. 
However, to increase production and productivity and thus growth rate of agricultural crops 
in the country, the Government is implementing centrally sponsored Integrated Cereal 
Development Programmes in rice/wheat/coarse cereals Based Cropping System Area, 
National Pulses Development Project etc. Under these programmes/project, incentives 
are provided to farmers for use of high yielding varieties of seeds, application of integrated 
pest management, propagation of scientific water management including micro irrigation 
and use of improved farm implements. Research is also being continuously undertaken to 
develop improved technologies so as to enhance the productivity and production of 
foodgrains in India. Field demonstrations on farmers` holdings including training of farmers 
and farm labourers is being organised for effective transfer of technology.

records.title: OUTSTANDING DUES AGAINST PRIVATE COMPANIES .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that after the declaration of new Communication Policy, 1999 certain companies functioning under private sector have not made payment of Government dues outstanding against them so far?
(b) if so, the names of such companies alongwith the amount of funds outstanding against them; and
(c) whether Government have also taken any action against them for not making the payment of outstanding amount, if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS
 (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR) 
(a) to (c)
Defaults in payment of license fee dues as per the prevailing license agreements had taken place before the declaration of the New Telecom Policy, 1999 (NTP-99).
The NTP-99 specifically provided for satisfactory resolution of existing operators` problems in a legally tenable manner consistent with their contractual obligations. Accordingly on 22.7.99 the government offered a package to existing cellular and basic services licensees to migrate to the revenue sharing regime under NTP-99. Under the terms and conditions. of this package the licensees had, inter-alia, to clear the dues outstanding on the cut-off date of 31.7.1999 within a specified time frame. Forty licensees of Cellular and Basic cervices came under the process of migration, and all of them have paid the dues in terms of the migration
package by the extended date(s).
Six cellular licenses were not covered by the migration package since by 22.7.99 these had been already terminated for non-payment of the dues. Further, two defaulting cellular licensees in Uttar Pradesh -(East) did not come under the process of migration because-one of them did not accept the package and hence an essential condition, that all the licensees in a Service Area accept the package, remained unsatisfied. Their licenses were not terminated In the absence of a fall back arrangement for their subscribers.
A modified migration package has been offered to seven of the above-mentioned eight license-holders in April 2000 with. enhanced penalties, etc. ` For the `eighth company (M/s. JT Mobile, Punjab) also it .has been decided, in principle, to offer a package for migration loathe revenue Sharing regime under NTP-99. The dues in respect of these eight licenses are given in Annexure.
On 2.9.99, a migration package was similarly offered to Radio Paging licensees. However, as the terms and conditions of the package were not fulfilled, implementation of the package did not proceed further and the outstanding dues continue to persist, as detailed in the Annexure.
Outstanding dues against other value added service providers are also indicated in the Annexure. The government has taken steps from time to time to realise the amounts due from the defaulters. These have included, inter alia, issue of notices, invocation and encashment of Bank Guarantees, and even termination of licenses.

details:
MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
( SHRI AJIT KUMAR PANJA)
(a ) It has been decided by mutual consultations to allow the US Embassy in New Delhi to augment its strength for opening a Legal Attache Office. Such offices are normally manned by two FBI Officers. Government of India has similar representation in its Embassy in Washington. There is however no proposal for setting up an independent office of the FBI in India. 
(b ) The decision was taken in February 2000 and the US Government is in the process of implementing it shortly.
(c ) The decision was taken in the context of growing Indo-US bilateral co-operation on counter-terrorism. While necessary mechanism to counter terrorism is already in place with the Extradition Treaty and the Joint Working Group on Counter-terrorism, the opening of the Legal Attache Office will enable more effective co-ordination between our law enforcement agencies. It will also signal greater commonality of interests between the two countries in the fight against terrorism. This will in turn exert pressure on extremist groups operating across borders.

records.title: POLICY FOR PROPER MANAGEMENT OF WATER .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that water crisis is deepening day-by-
 day in the country due to the shortage of water supply;
(b) whether Government would formulate a well planned and
 definite water policy for proper management of water in the
 country; and
(c) if so, by when and whether Government have identified the
 fundamental bases and priorities for preparing the water policy;
 if so, the details thereof ?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY) 
(a) to (c) The per capita water availability is reducing
progressively due to increasing population. It is estimated that
the average annual per capita water availability may come down
from about 1869 cu. m. at present to 1350 cu. m. by 2025 A. D. at
the national level. According to international criteria any
situation of yearly water availability or less than 1000 cu. m.
per capita is considered as scarcity condition. Therefore, even
by the end of 2025 A. D., India is not likely to face water
scarcity situation at the national level, though uneven water
availability may cause local water scarcity in some parts of the
country.
A National Water Policy already exists which provides for
planning and management of country’s water resources on a
sustainable basis. However, since the adoption of the National
Water Policy in 1987, a number of problems/challenges have
emerged in the development and
..2
..2..
management of the Water Resources Sector. As such, the existing
National Water Policy has been reviewed by the National Water
Board (NWB) in the context of existing problems/emerging
challenges and also in the light of the experiences of the last
13 years of its implementation. The updated draft National Water
Policy finalished by NWB in October, 1998 provides for multi-
sectoral perspective and participatory approach towards
resources planning and management; integration of quantity,
quality and environmental aspects and private sector
participation in the water resources management, mandatory
operation and maintenance, funding and related policies for
revenue generation; and reforms related to legislations,
institutions, environment and technology etc., under the Water
Resources Sector. However, declaration of the new National Water
Policy depends on its adoption by the National Water Resources
Council.

records.title: CRITERIA FOR UPGRADATION OF AIRPORTS .
details:
(a) what criteria have been set for selecting the places for
 upgradation of airports; and
(b) the names of the international airports which are
 operating in the country at present?

MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)
(a):- The criteria for setting up of international airports
are as under:
(i) There should be a demand for international operations;
(ii) There should be facilities for customs, immigration,
health, plant quarantine, etc.
(iii) The runway length should be minimum 9000 feet of
adequate strength for operation of Medium Capacity Low Range 
(MCLR) aircraft which constitute majority of the aircraft
now for international operations; and
(iv) Adequate communication, navigation and surveillance and

by Shri Siddhartha Sen to study the marketing of commercial time on the various

records.title: COST OF INDIGENOUS COAL
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that indigenous coal would become costly in 
comparison to the imported coal in the southern States of the country due 
to the decision taken by the Ministry of Railways for hiking the freight 
on coal;
(b) if not, what is the assessment made by Government in this 
regard; and
(c) whether Government have provided certain suggestions to the 
concerned departments for checking the import of coal, and if so, the 
details thereof ?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINES & MINERALS 
(SMT. RITA VERMA)
(a)to(c) The indigenous coal per therm is costlier than imported
coal at certain coastal areas in Southern India due to certain reasons
including high railway freight over long distances. Any decision to 
hike railway freight will further render indigenous coal costlier at such
locations in the country. The Ministry had written letters to Ministry 
of Railways and the State Governments that any further increase in railway
freight and the royalty rates would make Indian coal further uncompetitive.

records.title: . COMPUTATION OF RATE OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION
details:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN) ) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 146 FOR ANSWER ON 6.3.2000 
(a) to (d) The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is a monthly index compiled and released by Central Statistical Orgamsation(CSO) to measure changes in the volume of production in physical terms. In order to accurately reflect the growth rate in the industrial sector, the base period of the index has been changed from time to time to reflect the changing structure of the industrial economy. The latest revision has made the base year 1993-94 from the earlier base year l980-81. The revised indices were released on 27th May, 1998.
The revision of the coverage of items and industries as well as the technique of construction has changed. Consequently, 543 items have been included compared to 352 items in the earlier IIP (Base 1980-81).
m the revised series of IIP with the base 1993-94, the items were selected on the basis of the criteria that each item so selected should account for at least Rs. 80 crore of Gross Value of Output (GVO) at the overall manufacturing level and Gross Value Added (GVA) of Rs.20 crore at the ultimate digit level of NIC. The criteria were applied flexibly in the case of industry groups which were not adequately represented. Therefore, items of importance are included and unimportant items are dropped m the new item basket. The list of new item groups alongwith the corresponding individual items included in the revised series of IIP is enclosed.

details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE
 (SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL) 
(a) : India`s foreign exchange reserves, including gold and SDRs, as on February 18, 2000 amounted to US$ 35193 million, which is considered adequate, judged in terms of critical indicators such as, import cover of reserves and debt service payments. 
(b) : During the first ten months (April 1999 to January 2000) of the financial year 1999-2000, the level of foreign exchange reserves was maximum at US $ 35170 million on January 21, 2000 and it was minimum at US $ 32535 million on April, 1,1999. 
(c) : Movements in foreign exchange reserves reflect the net outcome of inflows and outflows of foreign exchange on account of transactions in the current and capital accounts of India`s balance of payments. Therefore, it is not possible to establish one-to-one correspondence between changes in reserves and movement in each of these transactions. However, it can be stated that the build up of foreign exchange reserves in the current financial year so far has been made possible largely because of sharp recovery of exports, buoyancy in invisible receipts, sharp turnaround in portfolio investments by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) and significant net accretions to Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits.

records.title: AGREEMENT BETWEEN AMERICA AND INDIA TO REMOVE RESTRICTIONS H
details:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)
(a)to (d): India has been maintaining Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on imports for Balance of Payments (BOP) reasons. In January 1997, following an improvement in its BOP position the `Committee on BOP Restrictions` of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) invited India to present a phase out Plan for elimination of its remaining QRs maintained for BOP purposes. India presented a nine year phase out plan for removal of its QRs, which was further reduced to seven years but even this was not acceptable to a number of India`s trading partners. Consequently, the Committee concluded its consultations without any decision.
Subsequently, India held consultations and signed bilateral agreements with Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Switzerland, European Union and Japan for a six year phase out of its QRs on BOP grounds by 31/3/2003. However, such consultations with USA did not fructify and the USA initiated a dispute against India in the WTO. The Dispute Settlement Panel and the Appellate Body ruled against India holding that India was not justified in maintaining its QRs on BOP grounds. Following adoption of these reports by the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB), a reasonable period of time (RPT) had to be determined for India to implement the rulings and recommendations of the DSB. The RPT can be determined either through arbitration where the maximum period normally granted is 15 months or through bilateral agreement between parties to the dispute. India and the USA have signed a bilateral agreement for determining the RPT, which would be of little over 18 months. As per the agreement, all the existing QRs on BOP grounds would have to be removed by 1/4/2001.

records.title: METHOD ADOPTED FOR GDP ESTIMATES
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS. 
(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)
(a)&(b): The estimates of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) are compiled using basic data available from different sources. The sources of data include agricultural output based on the area statistics, productivity and prices provided by the State governments, industrial and services statistics from Annual Survey of Industries and Enterprise Surveys, conducted specifically to collect these data, annual reports and budget documents of public sector undertakings and government departments. The data collection methods have remained more or less unchanged. Over the years deficiencies have crept in. Moreover, data about the same head collected from different sources have come to show considerable discrepancies.
(c)&(d): The Government has established a National Statistical Commission on 19.1.2000 headed by Dr. C. Rangarajan to critically examine the deficiencies of the present statistical system with a view to recommending measures for a systematic revamping of the system, so as to improve the availability and quality of basic statistics. There is also a proposal for modernising the Indian Statistical System with possible external assistance.

records.title: MILK PRODUCTION .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the production of milk in the country is
highest as compared to other milk producting countries of the world;
(b) if so, what is Government`s reaction in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that despite maximum availability of milk,
its produced quantity is less than its requirement in the country; and
(d) whether Government would consider to curb the export of milk and its
products; if so, the details thereof?

The Minister of state in the Ministry of Agriculture 
(Shri Hukumdeo Narayan Yadav)
(a)to (c) Yes, Sir.
The Indian council of Medical Research (ICMR) study indicates
220 gms. of milk per day per person as the recommended intake for Indians.
The 1997-98 availability of milk is 204 gms. per day per person. However, the
avialability of milk per capita per day has steadily increased from 173 gms.
in 1989-90 to 204 gms.in 1997-98. The gap between the requirement and the
availability is decreasing over years and it is expected that in the near
future we would reach 220 gms. per capita per day requirement.
(d) The Government has no proposal to curb the export of milk and milk
products.
